item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — A quad injury cost Jason Adam the chance to help the Padres in last year’s NL Wild Card Series. The team is intent on seeing what the 35-year-old veteran can provide this time around.
Out since late June with a shoulder injury, Adam was activated ahead of Wednesday’s 7:10 p.m. start at Dodger Stadium. To make room, right-hander Griffin Canning was optioned to Triple-A El Paso and reliever Alek Jacob was designated for assignment to allow Adam to rejoin the 40-man roster.
“We saw last year when he got hurt how much we missed him just within the team dynamic and what he provides as experience out there in the bullpen,” Padres manager Craig Stammen said. “We’ve got a lot more experience than what we had last year in the bullpen right now with those guys being together. But Jason’s a big part of that. He’s a big part of that group out there, and then he’s a pretty darn good pitcher also.”
A first-time All-Star last year, Adam allowed nine runs on seven hits and two walks over 1⅓ innings across three rehab appearances with El Paso. But both he and the team were satisfied with the stuff he showed in hitter-friendly conditions, as well as in live batting practice on Monday, and added his experience to a bullpen that was a strength last year and this year.
Adam’s velocity has trended down from about 95 mph the year the Padres acquired him in 2024 (1.95 ERA) to 94 mph last year (1.93 ERA) to 93 mph this year (2.51 ERA). He missed time earlier in the year as he returned from last year’s season-ending quad surgery and said Tuesday he was eager to get back in the thick of a postseason push.
“Yeah, I’d love to be part of every game,” Adam said after joining the team at Dodger Stadium on Tuesday. “What this team’s doing is really special. So I just want to fill my role, however that looks, and help them win ballgames. We’ve seen pretty well that this team’s good with or without me. I just want to do my part to contribute.”
Ousted from the rotation earlier this summer, Canning was better as a reliever (3.82 ERA in 35⅓ innings) than as a starter (6.79 ERA in 50 ⅓ innings) and had been critical in helping the team piece together games ahead of the trade deadline. But the team only needs three starters for the NL Wild Card Series, he was behind the likes of Robbie Ray, Casey Mize and Randy Vásquez in terms of depth arms for a short series and David Morgan has allowed one run in his last 7⅔ innings to seemingly cement his spot in the depth chart ahead of Canning.
The Padres optioning Canning to the minors means he cannot return to the active roster without an injury until the middle of the NL Division Series, after 15 days.
Jacob, 28, had a 5.58 ERA in 61⅓ innings at Triple-A El Paso and 4.18 ERA in 56 innings across parts of four seasons in the majors. He pitched in three games this year, allowing three runs in five innings as an up-and-down arm.
Ohtani returns, Salas starts
As expected the Dodgers reinstated Shohei Ohtani (biceps, knee from the injured list, as well as left-hander Tarik Skubal from the bereavement list. To make room, outfielder Josue De Paula and Hurt were optioned to Triple-A Oklahoma City.
Ohtani will bat second and serve as the designated hitter for the Dodgers, who have won eight of 11 so far against the Padres this year. Ohtani was 0-for-3 when he last played on Sept. 9 and was in a .122/.295/.184 slide over his last 13 games.
Tonight's #Dodgers lineup vs. Padres: pic.twitter.com/SyL3INJl9z
— Los Angeles Dodgers (@Dodgers) September 23, 2026
As for the Padres, Ethan Salas will get his first start at Dodger Stadium and second pairing with left-hander Robbie Ray. The only starter he has not worked with is Michael King.
Salas (.627 OPS) was 1-for-2 off the bench on Tuesday. He will bat ninth in a lineup that will see Samad Taylor (.856 OPS) get the start as the DH after Austin Hays did so on Tuesday.
Tonight’s lineup. pic.twitter.com/zLU04b89qh
— San Diego Padres (@Padres) September 23, 2026
While the Padres’ lead on the Diamondbacks was shaved from five to four games with five games left in the season — including three head-to-head matches in San Diego — Tuesday’s loss did little to diminish postseason odds, which are at 93.5% according to FanGraphs.com.
As was the case on Tuesday, any combination of two Padres wins and/or Diamondbacks losses will clinch the team’s third straight postseason berth.
Right-hander Merrill Kelly (9-14, 5.00 ERA) will start at Coors Field for Arizona against Rockies right-hander Mason Adams (0-1, 5.09 ERA). First pitch there is 5:40 p.m..
The Padres, Cubs and Phillies all began Wednesday with identical 87-70 records, although the Padres have to finish ahead of both teams to earn home games in the NL Wild Card Series as they lost both season series.
The Dodgers’ magic number to clinch a first-round bye over the Braves is 1. They are also one game ahead of the Brewers in the race for the NL’s No. 1 seed.
Glass half full
The Dodgers just about emptied the bullpen in Tuesday’s 7-0 win over the Padres. In the aftermath of another bullpen game slowing an offense that ranks first in the majors this month in OPS (.835), a half-glass-full view of what transpired was worth taking forward.
The Padres saw all but two relievers — Kris Bubic and Evan Phillips — in their first shutout loss since Aug. 25 and they still had two more games to wade through in Chavez Ravine.
“They’re really good bullpen arms, so the more you can see them, the better shot you have,” first baseman Ty France said late Tuesday night. “But just move on to (Wednesday) and try to put some better at-bats together.”
The challenge of a bullpen game is a hitter rarely sees a pitcher twice and the Padres are especially proficient when they see relievers more than once.
They rank 10th in the majors with a .712 OPS against relievers, but 17th the first time they see a reliever (.704) and first the second time they see a reliever (.998 OPS).
Right-hander Kyle Hurt was the only pitcher to finish two innings and he allowed just one hit and faced seven batters while taking down the sixth and seventh innings.
Left-hander Jack Dreyer and right-hander Edwin Diaz got through their frames without giving up a baserunner. The rest of the slate of relievers all faced five batters or less.
In short, things went about as optimal as the Dodgers could hope for from a unit ranks 12th in the majors with a 3.82 ERA.
“The Dodgers bullpen’s got some good arms in it,” Stammen said. “They’re bringing out guys that have really good stuff. But the best way to do it is to play a little small ball and try to beat them that way. We just didn’t have the opportunity to play that way and score one run at a time (after) we get down 4-0. That kind of eliminates that way of playing baseball. But you know, we’ve seen their arms now for the rest of the series, and hopefully that benefits us going forward the next two days.”
Wednesday’s pitching matchup
Padres LHP Robbie Ray (13-8, 3.60 ERA)
He’s got a 5.22 ERA in eight starts since the trade deadline. His last start (6 IP, 3 ER) was one of three quality starts as a Padre and a 6-to-2 strikeout-to-walk ratio was his best since the trade. Ray has a 3.81 ERA in 26 career starts against the Dodgers, but he has allowed 15 earned runs in 19 ⅓ runs over four starts over the last two years.
Here is how Ray has fared against current Dodgers:
Dodgers RHP Yoshinobu Yamamoto (14-8, 2.51 ERA)
He’s thrown a career-high 179 innings while allowing a career-low 5.7 hits per nine innings. His 14 wins are also a new career best. Yamamoto has a 3.76 ERA in seven regular-season starts against the Padres and a 1.35 ERA in three starts this season (20 (IP, 6 BBs, 22 Ks).
Here is how Yamamoto has fared against current Padres in the regular season:

item.title: [sbsun.com] Shohei Ohtani returns to Dodgers’ lineup – but in a new spot
item.dc:creator: Bill Plunkett
item.description: LOS ANGELES — Rested and refreshed, Shohei Ohtani returned to the Dodgers’ roster on Wednesday. How refreshed remains to be seen. “These aren’t things that there’s a clear answer to,” Dodgers president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman said after Ohtani was activated from the injured list before Wednesday’s game. “I think everyone, this time of year, is dealing with some stuff, and so it’s all on that continuum. Shohei says he feels back to where he was earlier in the year, which is great,
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — Rested and refreshed, Shohei Ohtani returned to the Dodgers’ roster on Wednesday.
How refreshed remains to be seen.
“These aren’t things that there’s a clear answer to,” Dodgers president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman said after Ohtani was activated from the injured list before Wednesday’s game. “I think everyone, this time of year, is dealing with some stuff, and so it’s all on that continuum. Shohei says he feels back to where he was earlier in the year, which is great, which is a good start.
“Now, it’s one thing to feel that way for any player coming back from the IL. As they are coming back, it’s important for them to feel that way and when you’re coming back, now the question is, as you start to load on real games and that intensity and that workload, it’s making sure that what we’ve done keeps guys in position to be at their best.”
Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said Ohtani is “considerably” closer to being at his best than he was before going on the IL two weeks ago with biceps and knee issues.
“I would say if he was a ‘5’, he’s probably an ‘8’ or a ‘9’ right now,” Roberts said.
He also returned as a ‘2.’
For the first time since Mookie Betts suffered a fractured hand when he was hit by a pitch on June 16, 2024, Roberts wrote Ohtani’s name in as the No. 2 hitter in the Dodgers’ lineup behind Betts.
Roberts said he plans to go with Betts-Ohtani against left-handed pitching (like the Padres’ Wednesday starter, Robbie Ray) and switch to Ohtani-Betts against right-handed pitching (like Thursday’s starter, Nick Pivetta).
“I just feel good about it,” Roberts said of the decision to use both players at leadoff. “It just makes it tougher to navigate versus left(-handed pitching). There’s a Mookie tax. If you want to get to Freddie (Freeman, batting fourth), there’s a Will Smith tax. I like that and versus a right-hander I like kind of flipping those two for the same reasons.”
In four starts as the leadoff hitter before Ohtani returned, Betts was 8 for 16 with four doubles and two home runs.
Overall, the Dodgers went 10-3 in the 13 games Ohtani missed.
SEE YOU SOON
In order to make room for Ohtani on the active roster, rookie outfielder Josue De Paula was sent to Triple-A Oklahoma City, where he made his Triple-A debut Wednesday night in OKC’s playoff game against Las Vegas.
De Paula is expected to rejoin the Dodgers for next week’s bye week and is still in the running for a spot on the postseason roster. Given a “runway” to get at-bats at DH in Ohtani’s absence, De Paula went 10 for 31 (.323) with five extra-base hits (three doubles, a triple and a home run). Perhaps most impressive, he walked 11 times in 42 plate appearances while striking out just five times.
“It was actually an easier conversation than you guys probably would expect, given how well he’s performed,” Roberts said of telling De Paula he was being sent back to the minors – however briefly.
“This was the original thought that once Shohei gets back, we’re going to send him out. We had a runway to give him, which we gave him and he performed more than admirably.”
By sending De Paula out on Wednesday, he will be eligible to be recalled in time for the first game of a best-of-five National League Division Series next week.
“He’s a part of the conversation and he’s earned that and that’s what I told him last night,” Roberts said.
Roberts said De Paula showed in his short audition that he is “a special hitter.”
“Doesn’t chase. Moves the ball forward. The threat of power. Lefties don’t faze him,” Roberts recounted. “Hitters don’t (usually) see the ball that quickly out of hand. It’s a gift. No moment is going to be too big for that kid (if he is on the postseason roster).”
PITCHING PLANS
In addition to activating Ohtani on Wednesday, the Dodgers activated starting pitcher Tarik Skubal from the bereavement list and sent right-handed reliever Kyle Hurt back to Triple-A.
Skubal is scheduled to make his final regular-season start on Friday night in San Francisco. Blake Snell came out of his bullpen session on Tuesday with no issues in the groin injury that forced him to leave his start last week after one inning. He is expected to start Saturday’s game in San Francisco as a final test before the postseason.
UP NEXT
Padres (RHP Nick Pivetta, 3-2, 3.30 ERA) at Dodgers (RHP Tyler Glasnow, 5-1, 3.46 ERA), Thursday, 7:10 p.m., SportsNet LA, TBS, 570 AM

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Josue De Paula sent down by Dodgers but 'special hitter' could still factor into playoff plans
item.dc:creator: Andrés Soto; USA TODAY

With Shohei Ohtani back in the lineup for the Los Angeles Dodgers on Wednesday, Sept. 23 against the San Diego Padres and manager Dave Roberts wanting to get a look at other players competing for a spot on the postseason roster, Roberts said the choice to option De Paula to Triple-A Oklahoma City was easier than it might've appeared on the surface. "This was the original thought," Roberts sai
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — Josue De Paula's first trial run in the big leagues has come to an end. For now, at least.
With Shohei Ohtani back in the lineup for the Los Angeles Dodgers on Wednesday, Sept. 23 against the San Diego Padres and manager Dave Roberts wanting to get a look at other players competing for a spot on the postseason roster, Roberts said the choice to option De Paula to Triple-A Oklahoma City was easier than it might've appeared on the surface.
"This was the original thought," Roberts said. "That once Shohei gets back, we were going to send (De Paula) out. We had a runway to give him, which we gave him, and he performed more than admirably."
Even that might be an understatement to how well De Paula played.
In a small sample size of 11 games, the 21-year-old showed a confidence and poise beyond his years in the batter's box, controlling the strike zone like a seasoned vet and drawing 11 walks. And once the hits started falling, De Paula showed how dangerous he can really be, mashing three doubles and a home run (his first MLB hit in Miami) while driving in seven RBIs and posting a 1.081 OPS across 31 at-bats. His last regular season game in LA on Tuesday may have been his best yet as De Paula went 2-for-3 with a walk and his first career triple in a 7-0, series-opening win over the Padres.
He's played so well, in fact, that Roberts is seriously considering him for the postseason roster.
"He's a part of that conversation," Roberts said. "He's earned that."
De Paula's value goes beyond the stat sheet, too. Whether he's flipping the bat and yelling, "I really do this!" to his teammates in the dugout after hitting his first career home run, flexing after driving in a go-ahead run on a double or just nodding his head after not chasing a ball outside the zone, there's a level of swag De Paula brings to Dodger Stadium that not only energizes his older teammates, but also captivates fans in attendance every time "Hypnotize" by The Notorious B.I.G. blares over the loudspeakers when the Brooklyn native walks up to the plate.
Per MLB rules, a player who has been optioned can be eligible to play in the postseason as long as his club did so at least 10 days before a series. Optioning De Paula Wednesday would make him eligible to play in the NLDS, Game 1 of which starts on Saturday, Oct. 3, exactly 10 days from now.
That gives the Dodgers flexibility to evaluate the rest of the players vying for a spot in October with limited at-bats to go around in their remaining five games. Roberts specifically mentioned that he wants to get more reps for Miguel Rojas and Kiké Hernández, but the player that De Paula is most directly competing with is probably Dalton Rushing. He's been on the IL since Sept. 5 with right elbow discomfort but is expected to be activated ahead of the final regular season series in San Francisco this weekend.
Rushing won't catch again this season, so his best shot at making the playoff roster is as a lefty bat off the bench, which is the role De Paula would also have, given that president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman mentioned they currently view De Paula as a DH until his defense develops and he can be the capable corner outfielder they believe he can be one day. The Dodgers are unlikely to carry both De Paula and Rushing in October.
But while Rushing, Rojas and Hernández try to make their case in the last few opportunities, De Paula's already made his impression on Dodgers brass.
"Josue's been awesome," Friedman said. "Injected some real-life energy into our team as we got into September and close out the regular season. He handled himself as well as he could possibly do. ... He's done everything he can to put himself in a position to be in the conversation for us as we make our postseason roster."
"He's just a special hitter," Roberts said. "Hitters don't see the ball that quickly out of hand. It's a gift. Just the ability to (not) chase, I think that lines up in the postseason and no moment's gonna be too big for that kid."
De Paula joins the Comets in the middle of the Triple-A playoffs, but Roberts has basically seen enough from the rookie. The onus now lies on the vets.
This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Josue De Paula sent down by Dodgers but 'special hitter' could still factor into playoff plans

item.content:encoded:
Por BETH HARRIS
LOS ÁNGELES (AP) — Shohei Ohtani conectó un hit en su regreso a la alineación de los Dodgers de Los Ángeles la noche del miércoles, después de perderse dos semanas por molestias en el bíceps derecho.
Bateó segundo como bateador designado contra el abridor zurdo de los Padres de San Diego Robbie Ray.
“No estoy esperando demasiado. Ha pasado un tiempo desde que juega, pero es bueno tenerlo ahí”, comentó el mánager Dave Roberts antes del juego.
Los aficionados ovacionaron a Ohtani cuando caminó hacia el plato con “Feeling Good”, de Michael Bublé. De inmediato conectó una línea al jardín derecho con un lanzamiento de Ray en cuenta de 2-1 y los aficionados volvieron a alborotarse. Ohtani fue puesto out en segunda base cuando Will Smith bateó un rodado para una jugada de selección del fildeador hacia tercera.
Mookie Betts estuvo en el puesto habitual de primer bate de Ohtani, donde ha estado desde que la superestrella ingresó a la lista de lesionados el 8 de septiembre.
Betts batea para .366 con seis jonrones, 21 carreras impulsadas, 13 bases por bolas y 18 carreras anotadas en 18 juegos en septiembre. Está empatado en el tercer lugar de las Grandes Ligas con 26 hits este mes, y también figura entre los líderes de la Liga Nacional este mes en hits de extrabase, carreras impulsadas, bases totales, dobles y carreras anotadas.
Ohtani jugó por última vez el 7 de septiembre contra Cincinnati y llegó bateando para .277 con 30 jonrones, 80 carreras impulsadas, 89 carreras anotadas y 80 bases por bolas en 134 juegos. En el plato se le vio físicamente limitado, sacudiendo el brazo y haciendo gestos de dolor en ocasiones.
“Hace unas semanas se podía ver que no podía batear una recta; se quedaba por debajo de todo y el swing era más lento”, señaló Roberts. “Controlar el swing, el punto de contacto, creo que eso es algo en lo que me fijaré y, obviamente, cosas como los gestos de dolor, pero no espero ver nada de eso”.
Los Dodgers concluyen su serie de tres juegos contra los Padres el jueves, y luego viajan a San Francisco para tres juegos contra los Giants para cerrar la temporada regular.
En otros movimientos, el lanzador Tarik Skubal fue reincorporado desde la lista por duelo. Está programado para abrir el viernes en San Francisco. El relevista Kyle Hurt fue enviado a Triple-A Oklahoma City.
El novato Josue De Paula fue enviado de vuelta a ligas menores; podría regresar para la postemporada
Con el regreso de Ohtani, Josue De Paula bajó a la Triple-A para unirse a los Comets en los playoffs de la Pacific Coast League contra los Las Vegas Aviators. De Paula había estado en la alineación como bateador designado.
De Paula se convirtió rápidamente en un favorito de los aficionados durante la ausencia de Ohtani. El neoyorquino de 21 años se embasó de manera segura en 10 de sus primeros 11 juegos en las Grandes Ligas. Se fue de 3-2 con una carrera anotada y una base por bolas, mientras conseguía el primer triple de su carrera en la victoria de los Dodgers por 7-0 sobre los Padres el martes.
___

item.title: [wfmd.com] Blue Jays’ Vladimir Guerrero Jr. says his $500M contract was for past performance – not future results
item.dc:creator: Latest; Breaking News

item.content:encoded:
Vladimir Guerrero Jr. has four games left before he can put his 2026 Toronto Blue Jays season behind him.
Guerrero, the six-time All-Star who signed the third highest-paid extension in MLB history in April 2025 at $500 million, has hit just nine home runs and slugged .359 to date for a career-low .695 OPS to date.
The Blue Jays, winners of the American League pennant this past season, where Guerrero was a major factor in reaching the World Series, were mathematically eliminated from this year’s postseason race as they hold a 77-81 record entering Wednesday.
For a player that is worth so much, especially financially, to an organization’s success, Guerrero’s down year has led to some vitriol from the Blue Jays’ fan base. And that’s likely to continue after hearing recent comments from the star infielder.
Guerrero, 27, sat down with Telemicro News recently, where he discussed his struggles at the plate this season, and how it reflects on his contract extension.
His comments were, well, interesting.
“The contract I got was based on what I did, not necessarily for what I’m going to do,” Guerrero said, as translated by MLB reporter Héctor Gómez. “I understand why the fans believe it’s the other way around. Sometimes, I think that way, too, like, ‘Oh, they give me this money, and I’m not doing enough,’ but you know I try my best, and I’m working hard.
“The fans, I know how they are, when you are doing great they are 100% behind you. But when you are not at your best, not everybody is behind you, almost nobody supports you. Those are my real fans, the ones that are supporting me all the time.”
After catching heat from Blue Jays fans, Guerrero was approached about the viral quotes, which he responded to.
“That was a quote from the interview when she asked me how I felt about this year,” Guerrero said, via MLB.com. “I said that, obviously, I feel really bad about the year that I had, that I couldn’t help my team get to the postseason. I said I felt – that it’s my personal opinion – that every player gets paid for what they have done. With that said, you guys have got to remember that I signed my contract at the beginning of last year, then I did put up a good year. Then, the kind of playoffs that I had to help the team get into the World Series.
“To the fans, I’ve never stopped working very hard. I am going to go into the offseason again to prepare myself the best I can. Physically, mentally, everything that I have like I always do for my team and my teammates.”
In Guerrero’s defense, that is technically what the Blue Jays did when they dished out his 14-year, $500 million extension, which is only behind Shohei Ohtani’s 10-year, $700 million deal with the Los Angeles Dodgers and Juan Soto’s 15-year, $765 million deal with the New York Mets. The franchise paid Guerrero for what he did from his debut in 2019 up to a fantastic 2025 campaign, where he belted eight homers and hit .397 across 18 postseason games.
But these comments show that Guerrero mustn’t be aware of what putting pen to money-filled paper meant in April 2025. No longer is it time in any sport, let alone Major League Baseball, where contracts are dished out based solely on past performance. It’s looking ahead to the future, where those past performances are expected to continue through a much-more lucrative deal.
MLB franchises sign players to contracts based on the market, and that market is justified by how the player will perform for them later on, while obviously looking at the track record in the past.
With any investment, those dishing out the big bucks want a return.
So, in a season where the home run total for a slugger is less than double digits – he still has time to at least get to 10 – and a career-low WAR (albeit the 2020 COVID-shortened campaign) has been accumulated, the Blue Jays and its fan base have every right to be disappointed. Yes, Guerrero was a major reason why Toronto reached the World Series in 2025, but the team and its fans are also allowed to voice displeasure with not just a down year – a career-worst performance in various metrics.
Would the Mets have dished out the highest-paying contract in league history if they didn’t expect Soto to continue performing at his superstar pace? No.
Would the Dodgers have agreed to give Ohtani $700 million, with heavy deferrals, might we add, to pay him for years without helping them reach their World Series goals? No.
From Mike Trout, to Mookie Betts, to Aaron Judge and the list goes on, every franchise wants to see a player they sign, especially for nine figures, to pay dividends. That’s the reality of the situation, whether Guerrero wants to view his deal as what he’s done in the past.
This is just one season, but Guerrero’s outlook needs to change just as much as his production moving forward on the remaining 13 years of his deal.

item.content:encoded:
Field Level Media

24 Sep 2026, 04:35 GMT+10

(Photo credit: Jayne Kamin)
The Los Angeles Dodgers activated two-way star Shohei Ohtani from the 15-day injured list prior to Wednesday's home game against the San Diego Padres.
Ohtani is in the lineup as the designated hitter and batting second behind Mookie Betts against Padres left-hander Robbie Ray.
Ohtani was on the injured list due to left knee and right biceps injuries. He also has been dealing with neck soreness.
Ohtani last played for the Dodgers on Sept. 7 and he hasn't homered or driven in a run in his past 13 appearances. He was 6-for-49 (.122) with 21 strikeouts during the span.
A four-time MVP, Ohtani has 30 homers and 80 RBIs in 130 games this season. The six-time All-Star is hitting .277 with a .380 on-base percentage and .522 slugging percentage.
In 14 starts as a pitcher, Ohtani has an 8-2 record with a 1.79 ERA, 95 strikeouts and 26 walks in 85 2/3 innings. He last pitched on July 3 and isn't expected to take the mound again this season.
The Dodgers optioned rookie outfielder Josue De Paula to Triple-A Oklahoma City in a corresponding move. The club's top prospect is batting .323 with one homer and seven RBIs in 11 games with Los Angeles.
--Field Level Media

item.dc:creator: Kiley Wren
item.description: Dodgers’ Ohtani set for return Wednesday after IL stint; Roberts says he’s ‘considerably’ better LOS ANGELES (AP) — Shohei Ohtani is expected to be back in the Los Angeles Dodgers’ lineup on Wednesday after a stint on the injured list. The two-way superstar has been on the IL since Sept. 9 due to right biceps inflammation and lingering soreness in his left knee. item.content:encoded:
Dodgers’ Ohtani set for return Wednesday after IL stint; Roberts says he’s ‘considerably’ better
LOS ANGELES (AP) — Shohei Ohtani is expected to be back in the Los Angeles Dodgers’ lineup on Wednesday after a stint on the injured list.
The two-way superstar has been on the IL since Sept. 9 due to right biceps inflammation and lingering soreness in his left knee.
Manager Dave Roberts said Ohtani is feeling “considerably” better.
“I would say if he was a five, he’s probably an eight or a nine right now,” Roberts said Tuesday before the Dodgers faced San Diego.
The Dodgers clinched their 13th NL West title in 14 years without Ohtani, who was in Los Angeles for treatment when the team beat Cincinnati on the road last week. Now, the four-time MVP will have five games remaining to get some at-bats in before the postseason begins.
Ohtani is likely to resume his role as the Dodgers’ leadoff hitter, especially against right-handed pitching. Mookie Betts has been atop the lineup and is hitting .373 this month.
“That’s probably the way it’s going to fall out, but I haven’t totally decided yet,” Roberts said, adding that he would consider Betts’ leadoff value against left-handed pitching. “I have to think about the entire lineup structure.”

item.title: [Dodgers Nation] Dalton Rushing Factored Into Dodgers’ Josue De Paula Demotion
item.dc:creator: Nelson Espinal
item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers catcher Dalton Rushing is the main reason red-hot prospect Josue De Paula was demoted. item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers catcher Dalton Rushing is the main reason red-hot prospect Josue De Paula was demoted.
The roster battle between Rushing and De Paula
For the postseason roster, Rushing and De Paula are competing for the last bench spot as a lefty pinch-hitter.
De Paula was sent down to Triple-A for the next week, opening a spot for Shohei Ohtani on the active roster.
Later on, Rushing will be activated and get his shot at the plate.
“It’s going to be a good debate,” manager Dave Roberts said to reporters. “Hitting off the bench is very difficult, and so you’re just trying to figure out who gives us the best chance.
“We have to have those conversations and make a decision.”
By demoting De Paula now, he can be added back to the active roster in time for the postseason if the team chooses him.
Where both Rushing and De Paula currently stand
Through 11 games in the big leagues, De Paul is hitting .323/.500/.545 with a 1.081 OPS. He is getting on base during half of his plate appearances, and he is really making hitters work.
On the other hand, Rushing has been on the injured list with an elbow injury.
He came back in early September, had four pinch-hit at-bats, and then went back on the injured list after his throwing program set him back.
With such obvious momentum for De Paula, the organization still wants to give Rushing a chance, though
“To be quite frank, it’s going to be tougher for Dalton given the time that he’s missed, and … you have three games to get back in the playoff form, which is tough to do,” Roberts explained
“It’s not a knock on him. He’s been great for us. But it’s still tough given that you’re also talking about the consistency of at-bats recently from Josue.”
Unless Rushing really puts something great together, Roberts and the Dodgers have no choice but to give De Paula a shot.
“Just showing them that I can swing it, and it’s an option,” Rushing told The LA Times after a recent batting practice.
“I know that you kind of tie [the team’s] hands up when you can’t play defense. So, I’m not expecting anything… just continue to take at-bats and see where we go from there.”

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Dodgers activate Shohei Ohtani, demote red-hot rookie Josue De Paula to Triple-A
item.dc:creator: Jack Baer
item.description: As expected, the Los Angeles Dodgers activated Shohei Ohtani from the injured list on Wednesday. In a corresponding move, they demoted a player who turned out to be a more capable replacement than anyone could've imagined for two weeks. That would be rookie slugger Josue De Paula, who was optioned to Triple-A Oklahoma City, a team whose season could end as soon as Wednesday. De Paula, the top prospect in the Dodgers' system and one of the best overall prospects in baseball, was promoted to repla
item.content:encoded:
As expected, the Los Angeles Dodgers activated Shohei Ohtani from the injured list on Wednesday. In a corresponding move, they demoted a player who turned out to be a more capable replacement than anyone could've imagined for two weeks.
That would be rookie slugger Josue De Paula, who was optioned to Triple-A Oklahoma City, a team whose season could end as soon as Wednesday. De Paula, the top prospect in the Dodgers' system and one of the best overall prospects in baseball, was promoted to replace Ohtani on the roster.
Ohtani will hit second in his first game back against the San Diego Padres, marking his first time not batting leadoff for the Dodgers since June 16, 2024. The red-hot Mookie Betts is filling the leadoff spot instead against Padres left-hander Robbie Ray.
De Paula, meanwhile, will be making his Triple-A debut as a starter for the Oklahoma City Comets in Game 2 of the PCL championship series.
In the 11 games Ohtani missed, no player on the Dodgers reached base more than De Paula. The Dodgers went 11-3 in that span and clinched both a playoff berth and the NL West while moving into strong position to secure a wild-card bye.
Between his cameo in L.A. and a performance in Double-A that won him Texas League MVP honors at 21 years old, De Paula has inspired questions about a place on the Dodgers' postseason roster.
As The Athletic's Katie Woo points out, De Paula being optioned on Wednesday means he will be eligible to be recalled by Oct. 3, when the Dodgers will begin playing the NLDS. He isn't technically eligible for the playoffs because he wasn't on the Los Angeles 40-man roster on Sept. 1, but that can be remedied by petitioning the commissioner's office for him to replace a player going on the injured list.
With Ohtani taking up the designated hitter spot and corner outfielders Teoscar Hernandez and Kyle Tucker both resurrecting down seasons over the past month or so, there's not a natural place for De Paula in the starting lineup.
Per The Athletic, De Paula is still in the mix for a postseason roster spot but appears to be in competition with Dalton Rushing for the role of premium left-handed bench bat. Rushing has been attempting to play through a partially torn UCL since early August. He won't be playing his usual catcher position again in 2026, but he could still hit.
Rushing is expected to be activated sometime this week, at which point he too will be trying to justify October at-bats in the final games of the regular season. De Paula has set a high bar to clear in that regard.
Figuring out where to put a rising star because your superstar is healthy again is ultimately a good problem to have. Whoever is on the roster, the Dodgers are on track to play the Atlanta Braves or Padres in the NLDS, though that could still change in the coming days.

item.title: [Dodgers Way] Dodgers demote Josue De Paula with a Dalton Rushing catch (but battle isn't over)
item.dc:creator: Matthew Swigonski
item.description: When the Los Angeles Dodgers called up Josue De Paula just a few weeks ago, there weren’t really any major expectations for him to carry the offense or make a huge contribution this season. He was here to get his cup of coffee and gain some invaluable MLB experience. But in his short time with the club, De Paula has made such a massive impression that he has already forced a potential postseason roster battle that could end up with him on top. As reported by Katie Woo of The Athletic, De Paula h
item.content:encoded:
When the Los Angeles Dodgers called up Josue De Paula just a few weeks ago, there weren’t really any major expectations for him to carry the offense or make a huge contribution this season. He was here to get his cup of coffee and gain some invaluable MLB experience. But in his short time with the club, De Paula has made such a massive impression that he has already forced a potential postseason roster battle that could end up with him on top.
As reported by Katie Woo of The Athletic, De Paula has become an unexpected yet good problem for the Dodgers as they are set to welcome back a number of players from the IL. The team activated superstar Shohei Ohtani after he had been dealing with a handful of nagging injuries.
The Dodgers will also look to activate catcher Dalton Rushing from the IL before the end of the regular season. While he will not be able to return behind the plate this year, the team could potentially use his bat off of the bench. This could lead to a log jam on the bench and a position battle between Rushing and De Paula ... down the line. To begin the proceedings, De Paula will go down on Wednesday in favor of Ohtani, while Rushing till ideally get some at-bats at the MLB level before the season ends.
This doesn't mean De Paula can be counted out of the postseason roster mix, though. That debate hasn't finished yet (or even begun until Rushing can get some reps).
While Dodgers manager Dave Roberts admitted earlier in the week that it could lead to a “good debate” as the team determines which of the two players to carry on the postseason roster, he may have already shown his hand.
“To be quite frank, it’s going to be tougher for Dalton, given the time that he’s missed, and to kind of think that you have three games to get back in playoff form, which is tough to do,” Roberts said of Rushing.
“It’s not a knock on him. He’s been great for us. But it’s still tough, given that also you’re talking about the consistency of at-bats recently from Josue. We have to have those conversations and make a decision.”
With just a handful of games remaining in the regular season, Rushing likely won’t get many at-bats to get back into a rhythm before the playoffs. Whether or not that will have the greatest impact on Roberts’ final decision will be interesting to watch out for. It will be hard to overlook how hot De Paula is at the plate right now though, even as he heads to the minors.
Josue De Paula has already become a force in the Dodgers’ lineup
Through his first 31 at-bats with the Dodgers, De Paula has already collected 10 hits and driven in seven runs. With a .323/.500/.581 slash line, he has shown that he’s capable of handling MLB pitching. Well, at least in the short term. We have seen rookies come up to the majors and wreak havoc at the plate before teams have time to collect enough tape on them and pitchers can make the adjustment.
Then again, as the Dodgers' No. 1 prospect, De Paula has raked at every level in the minor leagues. With a career .857 OPS in five minor league seasons, he has the tools to make the adjustments of his own. He already has an excellent grasp on the strike zone and plate discipline that rivals seasoned MLB veterans. De Paula has drawn 11 walks in 11 games in his young career in the bigs.
The postseason is obviously a different beast than a prospect’s first dozen MLB games. At-bats are more scrutinized and the pressure would be unlike anything De Paula has experienced in his pro career. He also lacks the experience of coming off the bench cold and pinch hitting, especially in high-leverage situations. But if anyone could overcome those obstacles, it is De Paula.
Despite Roberts already seeming to have a preference, De Paula isn’t a lock for the playoff roster quite yet. But with the ability to change the game with one swing, he could become one of the Dodgers’ most dangerous weapons off the bench in October.

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — The Dodgers on Wednesday activated Shohei Ohtani off the injured list on his first day eligible to return after the minimum 15 days on the sideline with right biceps inflammation. Josue De Paula was optioned to Triple-A Oklahoma City.
The plan is for Ohtani to be the designated hitter for the remaining five games of the regular season, to get him back in the swing of things at the plate. An accumulation of injuries ate into a very productive season for the four-time MVP. Left knee inflammation prevented Ohtani from pitching after July 3, and the right biceps injury started showing signs at the plate as well.
Ohtani last homered on August 18, part of a stretch of three home runs in two days at Coors Field. On that date, Ohtani was hitting .294/.390/.558 with a 153 wRC+, leading the National League in slugging percentage and OPS, and a close second to Pete Crow-Armstrong (155) in wRC+.
But in 13 games since, Ohtani had just six hits in 49 at-bats (.122/.295/.184) with 21 strikeouts and 10 walks. The Dodgers tried avoiding the IL, giving Ohtani four days off before returning on September 7, when he was hitless in three at-bats plus a walk, but aggravated the right biceps injury on a swing. That was the last straw that finally landed Ohtani on the injured list for extended rest.
“When he’s activated, he’s going to be in the best physical place he’s been in quite some time,” manager Dave Roberts said over the weekend, than on Tuesday added, “I would say if he was a five, he’s probably an eight or nine right now.”
Ohtani on the shelf opened a door for De Paula, the Dodgers’ top prospect, to get called up directly from Double-A. The Dodgers were hesitant to give De Paula playing time in the corner outfield, sticking with Teoscar Hernández and Kyle Tucker, who have each thrived in September. But with designated hitter open, De Paula had a chance to play every day, and he seized the opportunity.
De Paula has reached base in half of his 42 plate appearances, hitting .323/.500/.581 with three doubles, a triple, and a home run in his 11 games, and he has 11 walks against only five strikeouts.
“I think Josue has done a fantastic job,” Roberts said Tuesday.
Sending De Paula down to the minors means he won’t play in any of the Dodgers’ final five regular season games, but it doesn’t prevent him from making the postseason roster. De Paula needs to be on optional assignment for at least 10 days, a clock that does not stop for teams in the postseason. Getting sent down on Wednesday means his first day eligible to return is Saturday, October 3, which is the day of Game 1 of the National League Division Series.
He’s in a battle with Dalton Rushing for the left-handed bat off the bench, and De Paula has the built-in advantages that Rushing can’t really play in the field with the partially torn UCL in his right elbow, and that Rushing has been sidelined for two and a half weeks on the injured list.
“To be quite frank, it’s going to be tougher for Dalton given the time he’s missed, and to think that you have [three] games to get back into playoff form, it’s tough to do,” Roberts said Tuesday. “It’s not a knock on him, he’s been great for us, but it’s still tough, right, Given that we talk about having the consistency of at-bats recently from Josue. But we have to have those conversations and make a decision.”

item.content:encoded:
A los Dodgers les queda menos de una semana de la temporada regular para ponerse en forma para los playoffs. Y los movimientos en su plantilla para esta serie reflejan esa prisa por el tiempo.
El mánager Dave Roberts confirmó el martes que Shohei Ohtani (bíceps derecho, rodilla izquierda) iba a ser reincorporado el miércoles tras su estancia de 15 días en la lista de lesionados. Según Roberts, Ohtani se siente "considerablemente" mejor que antes de estar en la lista de lesionados.
"Diría que si antes estaba en un nivel de cinco, ahora probablemente esté en un ocho o un nueve", dijo Roberts antes de que ocho lanzadores lideraran la victoria de los Dodgers por 7-0 contra los Padres de San Diego en el primer partido de la serie.
El martes, los Dodgers redujeron a uno su número mágico para asegurar una exención en la primera ronda. Y antes del partido, recuperaron a otros dos jugadores importantes para la postemporada, al reincorporar del lista de lesionados al jardinero central Andy Pages (fractura en la mano izquierda) y al lanzador derecho Roki Sasaki (ampolla en el dedo medio derecho).
En movimientos correspondientes, los Dodgers enviaron al equipo de Triple A de Oklahoma City al lanzador derecho Emmet Sheehan y al receptor Eliézer Alfonzo.
Sasaki se hizo cargo de la cuarta entrada del partido con relevos y lanzó sin permitir carreras. Permitió un par de sencillos, pero su bola rápida tuvo un poco más de vida en esa breve participación, con un promedio de 98.7 mph y una velocidad máxima de 101.7.
"Pude adaptarme porque ya tenía la experiencia [desde el bullpen] del año pasado", dijo Sasaki a través del intérprete Kensuke Okubo. "Probablemente voy a lanzar en un par de partidos más, así que solo voy a hacer ajustes y seguir avanzando".
Pages se fue de 0 de 2, pero llegó a base dos veces, gracias a un golpeado por lanzamiento y una base por bolas.
"Obviamente, al haber estado fuera un mes, no me siento del todo bien ni tan cómodo al bate", dijo Pages a través del intérprete del equipo, Juan Dorado. "Pero hay cosas [de batear con la máquina Trajekt] que me ayudaron a poder regresar".
Sin embargo, incluso con el regreso de los jugadores, aún hay preguntas que los Dodgers deben responder en la última semana de la temporada:
¿En qué posición bateará Ohtani?
Al menos al principio, Roberts planea colocar a Ohtani al inicio del orden de bateo, como de costumbre. Pero el campocorto Mookie Betts ha entrado en la discusión.
"Sin duda, contra lanzadores diestros [Ohtani] estará ahí", dijo Roberts. "Creo que debería analizar la situación de Mookie contra lanzadores zurdos, pero tengo que pensar en la estructura completa de la alineación".
Ohtani ha sido el primer bateador en todos los partidos que ha sido titular este año. Pero bateó en el segundo lugar en 79 partidos entre las dos temporadas anteriores combinadas.
Incluso sin Ohtani, la alineación de los Dodgers ha estado funcionando bien. El martes, Tommy Edman conectó su segundo jonrón en otros tantos partidos, y Will Smith conectó un jonrón por tercera vez en cuatro días.
¿Está sana la rotación?
El lanzador zurdo de los Dodgers, Blake Snell, quien salió de su apertura la semana pasada por una contractura en la ingle izquierda, realizó una sesión de bullpen el martes. Está programado para una última apertura en la temporada regular el sábado, dijo Roberts.
Eso significa que los cuatro abridores proyectados de los Dodgers para los playoffs están programados para lanzar de este miércoles a sábado, con Yoshinobu Yamamoto y Tyler Glasnow en el montículo para los dos últimos partidos contra los Padres, y Tarik Skubal y Snell en los dos primeros partidos en San Francisco.
¿Quién es el cerrador?
En resumen, podría cambiar de un día para otro.
"En un mundo perfecto —aunque todos sabemos que el mundo no es perfecto—, me encantaría tener [un cerrador fijo]", dijo Roberts. "Creo que si surge la oportunidad, por ejemplo, de que Tanner [Scott] lance una entrada decisiva en la séptima u octava entrada, es difícil dejar pasar esa oportunidad si él es la mejor opción en ese momento. Porque simplemente no sabes cómo se desarrollará la novena entrada.
"Esas son cosas con las que hay que lidiar, y siempre es bueno que la gente las discuta. En este momento no veo a un cerrador que sea solo una persona".
Sasaki asumió ese papel el año pasado. No está claro exactamente cómo lo utilizará Roberts esta vez, pero Roberts dijo que podría ser una opción, dependiendo de cómo lance al regresar de la lista de lesionados.
"El año pasado fue una de esas situaciones de necesidad, dada nuestra situación en cuanto al rendimiento, la salud y la plantilla", dijo Roberts. "Desempeñó ese papel de manera admirable".
El martes, fue uno de los ocho lanzadores de los Dodgers que, en conjunto, lograron una blanqueada en un día de bullpen.
"Hemos tenido mucho talento a lo largo de los años", dijo Roberts. "Pero al sentarnos aquí hoy, al final de la temporada, el bullpen está en la mejor forma en la que ha estado. Eso podría cambiar en un día, en un partido, como todos sabemos. Pero en este momento, me siento muy bien con todos los que están ahí afuera".
El lanzador derecho Edwin Díaz, quien perdió el puesto de cerrador debido a una combinación de lesiones y bajo rendimiento, está en camino de volver a ser considerado para la novena entrada. El martes, retiró a los primeros bateadores de la alineación en orden para una quinta entrada limpia, lo que marcó su tercera salida consecutiva sin permitir carreras desde que regresó de la lista de lesionados.
"Si eres uno de los 12 o 13 lanzadores en una posible lista para la postemporada, estás en la lista de los que gozan de confianza", dijo Roberts. "Y él se ha colocado justo en medio de esa conversación. Y considerando todo lo que ha tenido que pasar este año para enderezar el rumbo, es un gran mérito para él".
¿Quién se queda con el último lugar en la banca?
La contienda por ser el bateador zurdo de la banca en la postemporada se ha reducido al novato Josué De Paula y al receptor lesionado Dalton Rushing (distensión en el flexor derecho). Pero con Rushing aún en la lista de lesionados, De Paula parece tener ventaja.
No le des demasiada importancia al movimiento correspondiente de los Dodgers con respecto a Ohtani el miércoles. Si envían a De Paula a las ligas menores a 10 días del primer partido de la Serie Divisional de la Liga Nacional, aún puede ser incluido en la plantilla.
Los Dodgers tendrán que hacer otro movimiento en la plantilla más adelante en la semana, cuando planean activar a Rushing. Si envían a un jugador a las ligas menores para hacerle espacio a Rushing, ese jugador solo sería elegible para el inicio de la Serie Divisional de la Liga Nacional como transacción correspondiente a un movimiento a la lista de lesionados.

item.content:encoded:
La recta final de la Temporada 2026 está al rojo vivo en las Grandes Ligas de Béisbol (MLB) y este miércoles 26 de septiembre los Dodgers se enfrentan a los Padres en el Dodger Stadium, desafío que representa el regreso de Shohei Ohtani a la alineación de los campeones defensores. Aquí te decimos dónde ver el juego de hoy EN VIVO.
Dave Roberts y los Dodgers viven una jornada especial ya que, finalmente, podrían asegurar ser uno de los dos mejores campeones divisionales en la Liga Nacional y evitar jugar la Serie de Comodines; todo esto ante unos Padres que, pese a una buena racha, necesitan ganar urgentemente para no rezagarse en la carrera por los puestos de playoffs.
¿Cómo llegan al juego Dodgers y Padres HOY?
Los Angeles Dodgers están teniendo un gran cierre de temporada llegando a esta jornada con 5 juegos ganados en fila, el más reciente blanqueando a los Padres por 7-0 durante un juego de bullpen. El de hoy representa un día especial para los Dodgers por el regreso de Shohei Ohtani de la lista de lesionados; el manager aseguró que está “significativamente mejor” tras presentar molestias en la rodilla izquierda y el bíceps derecho.
A shutdown performance from the 'pen. ???? pic.twitter.com/JPJbMfqkWO
— Los Angeles Dodgers (@Dodgers) September 23, 2026
Los San Diego Padres tuvieron que guardar la champaña ya que, al sufrir su segunda derrota en los últimos 15 juegos, se les negó su clasificación oficial a los playoffs, boleto que buscarán reclamar esta noche. Para ello, necesitan ganar esta noche ante los Dodgers y que los Diamondbacks caigan ante los Rockies.

item.dc:creator: Curt Bishop; Unknown

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are still battling it out with the Milwaukee Brewers for the top seed in the National League. Likely, whichever team captures the top seed will also have home-field advantage throughout the World Series.
Los Angeles is just one game behind Milwaukee for the top spot with five games left on the schedule. Though not surprising given the depth of their roster, the Dodgers have still been able to do this with Shohei Ohtani on the shelf with a knee injury. However, the two-way star is likely to return from the injured list on Wednesday, which should impact the Dodgers and the playoff race.
How Ohtani's return impacts Dodgers, playoff race
With the Dodgers just one game back of the Brewers for the top seed, this could give them a major advantage. Now, they have the best player in all of Major League Baseball healthy again, and with an upcoming weekend series with the 65-93 San Francisco Giants, they could have the advantage as they look to take the top seed.
Meanwhile, the Brewers, while facing a fellow non-contender in the St. Louis Cardinals, have the tougher scene facing up and coming pitchers Michael McGreevy and Quinn Mathews. Both the Brewers and Dodgers have already punched their tickets to the postseason, but if these two teams meet again in the NLCS, the Dodgers will almost certainly have the advantage with Ohtani back in action.
That gives their lineup a completely different look, and though Ohtani is likely done pitching for the year, the Dodgers lineup looks much better with him in it. As long as he can stay healthy in the playoffs, the Dodgers should be in good shape as they look to secure a three-peat.
Ohtani has been out a while too, so he should be quite well rested as he returns to action. The Dodgers are still a solid team without him, but they may now have the advantage as far as gaining the top seed in the playoffs, and this only further cements them as the favorite to win a World Series title
The two-way superstar is hitting .277/.380/.522 with 30 home runs, 80 RBI, a 6.5 WAR and a .902 OPS. Despite the injuries, he still has put together a solid season, and though he may not win the MVP this year, he still is among the most impactful players in the sport, and the Dodgers should have a big advantage with him healthy again.
Curt Bishop is a freelance sports writer who graduated from Maryville University of St. Louis with a Bachelor of Arts degree in the field of Communication and currently writes as a contributor for various platforms covering Major League Baseball. Curt’s work includes covering trade and free agency predictions, as well as rumors and news. La superestrella japonesa se espera que regrese este miércoles a la alineación de Los Ángeles después de permanecer en la lista de lesionados desde el 9 de septiembre por una inflamación en el bíceps derecho y dolor persistente en la rodilla izquierda.

Todo apunta a que retomará su lugar como primer bate, especialmente ante lanzadores derechos, aunque Roberts todavía analiza la estructura de la alineación y el papel de Mookie Betts, quien ha tenido un gran rendimiento durante septiembre

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] “Take Pressure Off Shohei Ohtani” – MLB Analyst Explains What Dodgers Should Do With Mookie Betts Once Injured DH Returns
item.dc:creator: Krutik Jain

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers' leadoff spot could be a toss-up between Mookie Betts and Shohei Ohtani come postseason. While Ohtani has done an exceptional job at the top for most of the season, his latest injury concerns and a drop in performance lately have made an MLB analyst wonder if the Dodgers should consider giving the job to Betts in October.
Betts is having a great month in September, batting .373/.468/.746 with six home runs, and posting a 1.215 OPS, 227 wRC+, and 1.6 fWAR. Betts' stellar hitting and previous success at the leadoff spot have former MLB player Xavier Scruggs convinced the Dodgers need to make the move and take the pressure off Ohtani.
"It takes pressure off Ohtani, putting him in the two-spot," Scruggs said of Betts. "And I think it's a real decision for Dave Roberts because, look, before Ohtani went on the IL, and it's almost like you don't know exactly what to expect once he comes back. So maybe that's a situation where, since his numbers have dropped, we ease it on him."
Ohtani's numbers were really off in the last 13 games before he hit the injured list. The Dodgers star batted just .122/.295/.184 with just one extra-base hit and struck out 21 times.
The contrast in performance could give Dodgers manager Dave Roberts a small headache before finalizing his postseason lineup.
When Can Dodgers Expect Shohei Ohtani to Return?
Shohei Ohtani will return to the Dodgers lineup on Wednesday against the San Diego Padres. Manager Dave Roberts confirmed he is ready to be reinstated from the 15-day injured list.
Ohtani will return as designated hitter, as he has already been shut down as a pitcher for the remainder of the season. The Dodgers superstar was suffering from right biceps inflammation and lingering left knee soreness, prompting his move to the injured list.
Ohtani is expected to resume hitting at the top of the lineup, though there are discussions about whether he could play behind Mookie Betts against left-handed pitching.
"That's probably the way it's going to fall out, but I haven't totally decided yet," Roberts said. "I have to think about the entire lineup structure."
The Dodgers have already clinched the NL West title and are strongly putting their foot forward to complete a World Series three-peat. Ohtani's return just before the postseason is to ensure the Japanese star gets some game time and finds his form at the plate.

item.title: [newsonjapan.com] Asian Games Day 5 Brings Swimming Gold and Gymnastics Drama
item.description: NAGOYA - Japan's Asian Games campaign produced another day of records and medals on September 23, with Shoon Mitsunaga setting a national record to win the men's 100-meter butterfly, both Japanese gymnastics teams taking silver behind China, and Toshikazu Yamanishi adding to the host nation's athletics medal haul. item.content:encoded:
NAGOYA - Japan's Asian Games campaign produced another day of records and medals on September 23, with Shoon Mitsunaga setting a national record to win the men's 100-meter butterfly, both Japanese gymnastics teams taking silver behind China, and Toshikazu Yamanishi adding to the host nation's athletics medal haul.
Away from the Games, the professional baseball pennant races entered their final stages, with Hanshin fighting to retain its Central League lead and SoftBank approaching the Pacific League championship.
The fifth day of the Asian Games brought a particularly intense contest between Japan and China, whose athletes met in swimming, gymnastics and athletics. China's 13-year-old swimming sensation Yu Zidi completed a remarkable hat trick of individual gold medals, while its men's and women's gymnastics teams narrowly defeated Japan in front of home spectators.
Japan's September 23 sporting program extended well beyond the principal medal events, with competition across rowing, fencing, table tennis, shooting, cycling, combat sports and a wide range of other disciplines. The Asian Games will continue through October 4, with athletics beginning its seven-day program in Nagoya.
Japan's swimming successes were led by 21-year-old Mitsunaga, who won the men's 100-meter butterfly at Tokyo Aquatics Centre in 50.56 seconds, lowering the Japanese record from 50.81. Defending champion Katsuo Matsumoto also reached the podium, taking bronze and giving Japan two medals in the event.
The result was particularly striking given Mitsunaga's performance in the morning heats, when he qualified seventh in 52.54 seconds. His improvement in the final brought Japan its second successive Asian Games gold in the event.
Japan added three silver medals and another bronze in the pool. Rio Shirai finished second in the women's 100-meter backstroke, while 35-year-old Satomi Suzuki collected silver in the women's 100-meter breaststroke in a Games-record time of 1:05.83. Komi Kato took bronze in the same event, and Japan's mixed 4x100-meter medley relay team finished second. Suzuki's result was her 11th career Asian Games medal.
China's Yu Zidi provided the day's other major swimming story. The 13-year-old won the women's 400-meter individual medley in 4:28.56, setting a Games record and completing three victories in three individual events after earlier winning the 200-meter butterfly and 200-meter individual medley.
China also won the men's 200-meter freestyle through Zhang Zhanshuo and the women's 100-meter backstroke through Peng Xuwei.
Japan's gymnastics teams experienced remarkably similar outcomes in their two team finals, finishing second to China in both competitions.
In the men's final, China scored 259.095 points, finishing just over one point ahead of the Japanese team. Zhang Boheng secured the title with a strong horizontal bar routine after Japan had entered the final rotation with a chance to overturn China's lead.
Olympic champion Shinnosuke Oka, competing with a back injury, fell during his horizontal bar routine and received 12.966. Teammate Daiki Hashimoto produced strong performances on pommel horse and vault, but China retained the Asian Games team title for a third consecutive edition.
Japan also took silver in the women's competition, scoring 165.362 points against China's 166.462. The Japanese team comprised Aiko Sugihara, Rina Kishi, Misa Nishiyama, Mana Okamura and Haruka Nakamura. It was Japan's ninth successive Asian Games medal in the women's team event.
The results followed Sugihara's individual all-around gold on September 22, the first by a Japanese woman at the Asian Games. The women's team will now turn its attention to the world championships in the Netherlands in October.
Soft tennis supplied two more gold medals for Japan. Toshiki Uematsu won the men's singles title, with fellow Japanese player Takuya Kurosaka taking silver, while Reina Tenma captured the women's singles championship.
Japan also secured medals across several less-publicized sports. Nanoka Kida took silver in the women's jianshu and qiangshu combined event in wushu. The equestrian eventing team earned silver, with Olympic veteran Yoshiaki Oiwa adding an individual bronze, while cyclist Yudai Todome finished third in the men's road race.
Athletics opened its program with the men's and women's half-marathon race walks. Japan's two-time world champion Toshikazu Yamanishi finished second in the men's competition behind China's Shi Shengji, who broke away after the 10-kilometer mark. China also won the women's race through Yang Liujing.
The athletics program, running through September 29 at Mizuho Park in Nagoya, will bring further Japanese contenders into action as track and field joins swimming, gymnastics and other established medal-producing sports.
Japan's team-sport campaigns also advanced significantly on September 23. The men's under-21 soccer team defeated Thailand 3-0 at Toyota Stadium to complete the group stage with three victories and no goals conceded. Yotaro Nakajima opened the scoring in the 31st minute before Keita Kosugi and Hisatsugu Ishii added two goals in quick succession early in the second half.
Japan had previously beaten Hong Kong 2-0 and Kyrgyzstan 7-0. The victory over Thailand secured first place in Group A and set up a September 26 quarterfinal against North Korea, which qualified from Group B after defeating Iran 4-1. Japan is seeking its first men's Asian Games soccer title since 2010.
The women's table tennis team also reached the final, defeating South Korea 3-0 in its semifinal at Sky Hall Toyota. Hina Hayata and Miwa Harimoto were among the players who helped Japan advance to a second consecutive Asian Games team final. Japan will face defending champion China on September 24, seeking its first women's team gold since the 1966 Bangkok Games.
Asian Games baseball produced another emphatic Japanese result as the corporate-league national team defeated the Philippines 7-0 at Toyohashi Municipal Stadium.
Japan scored twice in the second inning and three times in the third before adding another two runs in the sixth. Koya Yano and Masami Soeda each hit a two-run home run, while starting pitcher Kenta Nagano and reliever Kato combined to hold the Philippines to three hits. Japan completed its opening-round campaign unbeaten after earlier defeating China 11-3 and Palestine 15-0.
The three victories gave Japan first place in Group A and a place in the Super Round on September 25 and 26. The medal games are scheduled for September 27. Japan is attempting to win its first Asian Games baseball gold since 1994.
Japan's rowing team also reached an important milestone, with all 10 of its entered boats qualifying for their respective A finals despite heavy rain forcing changes to the competition schedule at the Nagaragawa International Regatta Course in Gifu Prefecture. The medal races are scheduled for September 24.
Outside the Asian Games, Hanshin strengthened its position at the top of the Central League with an 8-4 victory over Yakult at Jingu Stadium, extending its winning streak to four games.
Haruto Takahashi pitched six innings, allowing one run on five hits to record his league-leading 15th victory. Thirteen of those wins have come away from home, making him the first Hanshin pitcher to achieve that mark since Minoru Murayama in 1965.
The result was particularly important after the Tigers entered the day with a 1.5-game advantage over Yomiuri and a championship magic number of eight. The Giants remained in contention with a 2-1 victory over Hiroshima at Mazda Stadium.
SoftBank also moved closer to the Pacific League title, defeating Seibu 10-3 at Mizuho PayPay Dome in Fukuoka. The Hawks' latest victory came as Nippon-Ham lost 5-3 to Rakuten at Es Con Field Hokkaido. Orix defeated Lotte 1-0 at ZOZO Marine Stadium, with Ryoma Ikeda hitting his first career home run to provide the game's only run.
The day's other Central League result was a 4-3 victory for DeNA over Chunichi at Yokohama Stadium.
Soccer's domestic cup competition added another dimension to the day's schedule, with the Emperor's Cup continuing on September 23. All six J1 clubs facing J2 opposition advanced, including Kashima Antlers, for whom 18-year-old Minato Yoshida scored his first goal. Kashiwa Reysol also progressed with a victory over FC Imabari.
Grand sumo's September tournament reached its 11th day at Ryogoku Kokugikan, where yokozuna Onosato strengthened his position at the top of the championship race with a victory over sekiwake Fujinokawa. Onosato improved to 10 wins and one defeat, opening a two-victory advantage after all three wrestlers who had entered the day with two losses were beaten.
Ozeki Aonishiki defeated Takanosho to secure his eighth victory and a winning record. Sekiwake Atamifuji suffered his third defeat against ozeki Kirishima, while former ozeki Asanoyama improved to 8-3 with a victory over Kinbozan. With four days remaining, Onosato led a group of six wrestlers on three losses.
In Major League Baseball, attention surrounding Shohei Ohtani shifted toward his expected return to the Los Angeles Dodgers lineup after a spell on the injured list. Manager Dave Roberts confirmed on September 22 that Ohtani was scheduled to be reinstated on September 23 following treatment for knee and biceps problems. The Dodgers had already secured the National League West title and were preparing for the postseason.
Japan's September 23 sports program illustrated the breadth of the country's increasingly crowded autumn calendar, from national-record swimming performances and Asian Games medals to domestic baseball pennant races, international soccer, professional sumo and Japanese athletes competing overseas.
The next day of Asian Games competition will bring Japan's women's table tennis team into its final against China, rowing's medal races and the opening apparatus finals in artistic gymnastics, with further opportunities for the host nation to add to its medal total.

item.title: [mlb.com] The teams no one wants to play in October
item.dc:creator: Travis Sawchik
item.description: The best teams over 162 games and the clubs nobody wants to see in October are not necessarily the same. The regular season and the postseason reward different things. Over six months, baseball is a test of skill and depth. The weakest links eventually get exposed. item.content:encoded:
The best teams over 162 games and the clubs nobody wants to see in October are not necessarily the same.
The regular season and the postseason reward different things.
Over six months, baseball is a test of skill and depth. The weakest links eventually get exposed. A team can survive a thin rotation, a shaky middle-relief corps or a few light-hitting positions for a while – but it's much harder to hide those weaknesses over six months.
October is different.
The games are fewer, off-days greater. The urgency is heightened. Teams concentrate work among their best pitchers and lineups. Managers can shorten games with their best relievers. And one superstar hitter or ace can have an outsized influence on a short series.
Variance matters, too. A cleanup hitter can go 2-for-20 in April and the season keeps moving. Go 2-for-20 in October and the season might be over.
“Scary” is not necessarily the same as “best.” It is about concentration of talent, the ability to hide weaknesses, who is peaking at the right time, and the number of ways a team can make a short series tilt quickly.
I started with a simple framework: Which teams can shorten a series with two or three dominant starters? Which have a bullpen capable of essentially ending a game after five or six innings? Which lineups have enough power to avoid having to string together three or four hits against elite pitching? Which teams have deeper lineups to grind down opponents?
Who are the teams nobody wants to see in October?
The concentrated dynamo: the Dodgers
The Dodgers are the obvious answer.
Yes, they have some health question marks with Blake Snell and Shohei Ohtani. Yes, Edwin Díaz has not been the end-game piece they were hoping for in the bullpen. And, yes, their overall team slugging is down double-digit points from each of the last two years as well. But they are still a heavy World Series favorite no one wants to play.
A rotation led by Snell, Tarik Skubal, Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Tyler Glasnow is as good as it gets, and they are backed by a lineup that, while aging, still ranks as one of the best in the game. The market and models still believe they are the team to beat; FanGraphs gives them a 29.3% chance to win the title.
The team without a weakness: Brewers
While the Dodgers are the favorites, there's a case to be made that the Brewers are the scarier October opponent.
And after struggling out of the gate, Milwaukee is 82-44 since May 1 – five games better than the Rays, the next-ranking team. They've been above average in every month since April.
The terrifying thing about the Brewers is that there isn't an obvious way to attack them.
They have the most dominant pitcher in the game this year in Jacob Misiorowski, who unlike in his rookie year has shown no signs of slowing down. Misiorowski remains dominant in the second half with a 29% K-BB mark. His elevated velocity has held steady. And nearly as unhittable in the second half is Logan Henderson, who sports a 2.22 ERA, is holding opponents to a .171 average, and enjoys a 26.9 K-BB% mark since the All-Star break.
Getting the starter out doesn't make life easier either. The Brewers' reliever corps ranks fourth in ERA (3.41) and third in fWAR (6.6) out of all 30 teams.
Supporting those arms is an excellent defense.
And while the Brewers lack elite power, they string together quality at-bats with seven qualified Brewers hitters having an OPS+ of 100 or better, trailing only the Dodgers (eight) in the projected postseason field. The Phillies, by contrast, have two.
They are also trending the right way. The Brewers are 17-9 over the 30 days, tied for the second-best mark in baseball.
FanGraphs gives the Brewers the second-best title chances after the Dodgers (13.9%). They are a team built for the regular season and October.
OK, those are obvious contenders. What about other clubs?
The middling (potential) division winner: Guardians
The Guardians were one of the teams that actually won the Trade Deadline. Those added reinforcements, along with some positive regression from first-half slumpers like Steven Kwan, picked up a sluggish offense. They rank eighth in the Majors in runs since Aug. 1 (216 entering Tuesday).
A less obvious October advantage? Cleveland leads baseball in the percentage of plate appearances in which it enjoys the platoon advantage, at 77%, compared with a league average of 58.3%. In a five-game or seven-game series against a manager trying to optimize every matchup, that can become consequential.
And what really makes this team dangerous is the pitching staff.
The Guardians are one of three teams projected to be in the field that roster two pitchers that rank in the top 10 of fWAR in the second half of the season (the Dodgers are another, along with the Phillies).
Gavin Williams and Parker Messick have emerged as front-line starters this year. Tanner Bibee is a strong No. 3. While middle relief has hurt the club all season, being able to move a starter to the relief group should build a better bridge to closer Cade Smith.
Most teams that spend much of a season hovering around .500 don't have this kind of top-end pitching.
The Guardians are also hot, tied for the second-best record (17-9) in the Majors over the last month – tied with the Dodgers, Brewers, Braves and Padres – entering play Tuesday. Only the Rays (19-8) are better – but the Rays don't quite have the Guardians’ top-end starting pitching depth.
As the playoff picture stands entering Tuesday, the Guardians would face the winner of the White Sox (+42 run differential) or Rangers (-34 run differential) in the ALDS, with AL East clubs competing on the other side of the bracket. That's an extremely favorable path for a team with sneaky upside.
The unusual build: Cubs 
The Cubs are perhaps the strangest team on this list because their postseason case is built around the idea that an elite lineup and defense can overwhelm the quality and concentration of October pitching.
In the second half they've posted a 125 wRC+, 25% better than league average, and they've combined for a 134 wRC+ over the last month. That's an incredible number.
The 2018 Dodgers are an interesting comp. They led the NL with a 111 wRC+, including a 134 mark over the last 30 days of the season – just like these surging Cubs. They were also an elite defensive team lacking an elite rotation.
Those Dodgers won a relatively modest 92 games in the regular season but advanced to the World Series. Perhaps the Cubs can, too. While an ace makes life easier, there are different paths through October.
The wild card among wild cards: Padres
If you believe in timing and momentum, believe in the Padres.
For much of the season they have been a confounding team, much like their face of the franchise, Fernando Tatis Jr.
Over the last month, the Padres are third in baseball with a 118 wRC+.
Moreover, the pitching has become more interesting – deeper and healthier – at exactly the right time.
Nick Pivetta returned from his long absence to post a 1.93 ERA over three September starts.
Michael King has outperformed peripherals to become a 12-game winner with a 3.03 ERA. Robbie Ray, acquired at the Trade Deadline, gives them another veteran option.
They also have one great postseason advantage: If they can hand a lead over to the bullpen it's lights out with Adrian Morejon and Mason Miller closing out games.
The Padres own the end game, and at no time does that matter more than in October.

item.title: [Dodger Blue] Dodgers manager discusses intriguing postseason roster battle
item.dc:creator: Matt Borelli
item.description: Since being called up from Double-A Tulsa earlier this month as the corresponding move for Shohei Ohtani going on the 15-day injured list, Josue De Paula has done nothing but impress his Los Angeles Dodgers teammates and coaching staff. With Ohtani returning from the IL on Wednesday, questions remain about De Paula’s role with the
item.content:encoded:
Since being called up from Double-A Tulsa earlier this month as the corresponding move for Shohei Ohtani going on the 15-day injured list, Josue De Paula has done nothing but impress his Los Angeles Dodgers teammates and coaching staff.
The top prospect has flashed his elite offensive potential, showing remarkable plate discipline and power while drawing comparisons to New York Mets slugger Juan Soto.
With Ohtani returning from the IL on Wednesday, questions remain about De Paula’s role with the Dodgers moving forward. But the expectation is that he will compete with Dalton Rushing for the final spot on the team’s postseason roster.
“He’s done a great job,” manager Dave Roberts said of De Paula. “We made the move with Eliezer Alfonzo out on option with Andy (Pages) coming back. With Shohei coming back, I’m just not sure what the counter is going to be. But to your question, Josue has done a fantastic job.”
Rushing has been on the 10-day injured list since Sept. 6 after re-aggravating his right elbow while playing catch. However, he took live batting practice against Will Klein on Tuesday and should be activated in the coming days.
That would give Rushing only a few games to show the Dodgers he is back up to game speed and deserving of a spot on their postseason roster.
“Dalton, taking his at-bats. The thought is to give him an opportunity at some point in time to get activated and see how it looks coming off the bench,” Roberts said. “So I’m not sure if that’s tomorrow, Thursday, Friday, something like that.”
Rushing was in the midst of a breakout season before the right elbow injury threw him off course, so it will be interesting to see which direction the Dodgers decide to take.
Dodgers postseason roster battle
The Dodgers will consider several factors when choosing between De Paula and Rushing for the final spot on their postseason roster, including the ability to put together a good at-bat, not chasing pitches out of the strike zone and power.
“Quality of at-bat, conducting an at-bat, the ability to swing at strikes, take balls, get on base, get a hit,” Roberts explained. “There’s potential slug with both those guys. It’s going to be a good debate.
“I think hitting off the bench is very difficult, and you’re just trying to figure out who gives us the best chance. To be quite frank, it’s going to be tougher for Dalton given the time that he’s missed. To kind of think that you have three games to get back into playoff form, it’s tough to do. It’s not a knock on him. He’s been great for us, but it’s still tough.
“And also when you’re talking about having the consistency of at-bats recently from Josue. But again, we have to have those conversations and make a decision.”

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] How Can Dodgers Legally Get Josue De Paula On Postseason Roster?
item.dc:creator: Aaliyan Mohammed
item.description: In an unprecedented move in the Andrew Friedman era, the Los Angeles Dodgers called up a position player directly from Double-A earlier this month: Josue De Paula.
