item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are still fighting to keep their first-round bye, but they're already prepping for their 14th consecutive postseason appearance — and there are a number of questions they still need to answer.
Will Shohei Ohtani be ready? Does Edwin Díaz make the roster? Will Andy Pages be available? Is Roki Sasaki ready to return to his role as the Dodgers' vaunted postseason closer?
Every option to try to make up for these weaknesses is being considered. Even Hyeseong Kim, who has spent the majority of this season at Triple-A Oklahoma City.
"My expectation is Hyeseong will be here during the off-week and potentially be a conversation for the postseason — because he has the ability to run, play defense, and steal a base," Dave Roberts said, "So he's in the conversation, yes."
Alex Freeland is probably the most dispensable player on the Dodgers' active roster. If he's left behind, it'll be proof that their second base battle never truly declared a winner.
Dave Roberts hints at Hyeseong Kim return for Dodgers' postseason run
Kim was last seen in the majors from early April to late May. He was initially called up to replace Mookie Betts who went onto the injured list with an oblique strain. Kim hit .259 with a .651 OPS before being sent back down. His numbers in Triple-A have been nothing to write home about either (.675 OPS).
But Kim was on the Dodgers' postseason roster last season. His contributions were few — he earned a pinch-running appearance in the NLDS and was a defensive substitution during the World Series — and he didn't pick up a bat.
But Freeland is hot, and is hitting .375 with a 1.149 OPS over his last seven games. His ability to get on-base, the attribute that really put him on the map to begin with, has slowly come back to him. He has a .413 on-base percentage in September.
Clearly, this is a conversation the Dodgers are going to have to continue unless they trade one or both of these players. If Kim and Freeland survive the offseason together, they'll probably have to do it all over again next year.

item.title: [True Blue LA] Dodgers activate Andy Pages, Roki Sasaki from injured list
item.dc:creator: Eric Stephen
item.description: LOS ANGELES — The Dodgers on Tuesday got a few regulars back as reinforcements heading into the final week of the regular season and into October, activating center fielder Andy Pages and pitcher Roki Sasaki off the injured list. Pages missed 27 games after getting hit by a fastball on his left hand on August 21. Sasaki left his start in Atlanta five days later with a blister on his right middle finger. Emmet Sheehan and catcher Eliezer Alfonzo were optioned to Triple-A Oklahoma City on Monday.
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — The Dodgers on Tuesday got a few regulars back as reinforcements heading into the final week of the regular season and into October, activating center fielder Andy Pages and pitcher Roki Sasaki off the injured list.
Pages missed 27 games after getting hit by a fastball on his left hand on August 21. Sasaki left his start in Atlanta five days later with a blister on his right middle finger.
Emmet Sheehan and catcher Eliezer Alfonzo were optioned to Triple-A Oklahoma City on Monday.
Pages was an All-Star starter this season, and when he got hurt was tied with Yoshinobu Yamamoto for second-highest FanGraphs WAR (3.9) on the team, behind only Shohei Ohtani. By Baseball Reference WAR, Pages is still third on the team now at 5.4, trailing only Ohtani and Yamamoto. That’ll happen with a .272/.338/.458 batting line with a 118 wRC+ combined with plus-defense in center field.
Before getting hit by an errant fastball on August 21, Pages started 125 of the Dodgers’ 129 games, and led the team in plate appearances (550) at the time. Pages and Ohtani are still tied for the Dodgers’ lead with 80 runs batted in. With Pages out, Alek Thomas was first called up to start six games in center field, followed by Tommy Edman starting 17 games, plus three starts by Alex Call and one by Kiké Hernández.
With Edman moving to the outfield and once Thomas was optioned, Miguel Rojas (10) and Alex Freeland (eight) have covered all but one of the starts at second base in September.
Sasaki struggled earlier in the season, but improved as the season progressed. He has a streak of six straight starts with no more than two runs allowed until his blister start in Atlanta. On the season, Sasaki has a 4.46 ERA and 4.42 xERA, but since July 8 he’s down to a 3.25 ERA and 3.76 xERA in eight starts.
With Tarik Skubal, Yoshinobu Yamamoto, and Tyler Glasnow set for the postseason rotation, the Dodgers will see over the next two weeks if Blake Snell will be hampered by his left groin discomfort, and will have Sheehan at the ready. That allows them to use Sasaki in relief, as they did last postseason out of necessity.
“I could see multiples [innings], but it’s not going to be bulk as in four or five innings,” manager Dave Roberts said on Sunday.
Last season was a different situation for Sasaki, who struggled mightily as a starter and spend four months on the injured list before returning in the final week of the regular season. There was no room in the rotation, so he pitched in relief in the postseason. He wasn’t dominant — only six strikeouts among his 43 batters faced, with five walks — but he was effective, allowing only one run over nine appearances and 10 2/3 innings, the highlight his perfect three innings of relief in the Dodgers’ NLDS Game 4 clincher over the Philadelphia Phillies.
Sasaki saved three games last postseason. Roberts said Sasaki probably wouldn’t get an opportunity in a save situation right away this week, but it could progress to that by the postseason.
“I trust Roki in any situation. I would say probably starting a clean inning,” Roberts said. “He’s done it, he’s really good. He’s a neutral pitcher, high-octane stuff. And you really just need four starters. So we’re in a good spot there, for now.”
Sheehan has been fantastic of late, allowing only one run in three starts for the Dodgers over the previous two weeks, with 24 strikeouts in 17 innings. The plan for Sheehan is to start on Saturday for Oklahoma City should the Comets advance to the Triple-A championship game.
Alfonzo was back with the Dodgers since September 6 when Dalton Rushing was placed on the injured list with elbow soreness. In the 14 games since, Alfonzo played only once, pinch-hitting as the designated hitter at the end of a 14-1 blowout of the Cincinnati Reds. He struck out.
Alfonzo made his major league debut against the Padres on July 5, and started nine games behind the plate. He had five hits in 28 at-bats with three doubles and four runs batted in.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Dodgers Top Prospect Josue De Paula Explains Viral Encounter With Shohei Ohtani
item.dc:creator: Ricardo Sandoval; Unknown
item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers top prospect Jose De Paula was surprised to see Shohei Ohtani in the dugout during Friday's game against the San Francisco Giants. His face made that clear. De Paula said he didn't expect Ohtani to be in the dugout when he embraced his teammates after scoring a run for the Dodgers in the contest, leading to his viral reaction. “I actually seen him earlier that day but I wasn’t expecting him to be at the game," De Paula said. "He caught me by surprise, I was giving everybody a
item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers top prospect Jose De Paula was surprised to see Shohei Ohtani in the dugout during Friday's game against the San Francisco Giants.
His face made that clear.
De Paula said he didn't expect Ohtani to be in the dugout when he embraced his teammates after scoring a run for the Dodgers in the contest, leading to his viral reaction.
“I actually seen him earlier that day but I wasn’t expecting him to be at the game," De Paula said.
"He caught me by surprise, I was giving everybody a handshake, I gave him a handshake, but then I double take like he’s here.”
De Paula made his MLB debut on Sept. 11 after the Dodgers placed Ohtani on the injured list due to a variety of injuries he's been battling.
The 21-year-old is Ohtani's replacement in the lineup and serves as the Dodgers' designated hitter for now.
De Paula also mentioned that he is excited to see Ohtani back at the plate for the Dodgers.
“I can’t wait until he’s back. To see what he does in the box, you don’t see that every day so I can’t wait," he said.
In 28 at-bats as a Dodger, De Paula has recorded a .268 batting average with a .974 OPS, one home run, seven RBIs and one stolen base.
How Close Is Shohei Ohtani to Returning?
It hasn't been a pretty second half for Ohtani, as he battled with injuries for the better part of a month-plus.
Since the start of August, Ohtani's bat has gone ice cold.
From Aug. 1 until he was placed on the 15-day IL, Ohtani has a .231 batting average with 27 hits, six home runs, 13 RBIs and 19 runs.
While Ohtani's numbers are far below what is expected, the Dodgers hope that is a thing of the past.
Ohtani is eligible to return to the lineup Wednesday, and he's progressing well in his recovery. The 32-year-old took a major step this past weekend, as he was seen running the bases and hitting off the Trajekt machine.
Manager Dave Roberts said he hopes Ohtani will be ready to return Wednesday. If not, the four-time MVP could make his return Thursday.
Ohtani is in his third year with the Dodgers after signing a 10-year, $700 million contract in December 2023.
The two-way superstar has led the Dodgers to back-to-back World Series titles. While he isn't at 100% with the postseason nearing, he's expected to do his part to try to lead Los Angeles to yet another World Series title in 2026.

item.title: [Dodgers Nation] Shohei Ohtani Has 'Good Chance' of Returning to Dodgers This Week
item.dc:creator: Cameron Kiszla
item.description: It’s been weeks since Los Angeles Dodgers fans have seen a healthy and productive Shohei Ohtani in the lineup, but that wait could be nearly over. Ohtani could be activated as soon as Wednesday, reports Sonja Chen of MLB.com. That means Ohtani is likely to be playing in a couple of the games against the San Diego Padres in the last regular season home series of the season. “There’s a good chance next series we’ll see him,” manager Dave Roberts said. item.content:encoded:
It’s been weeks since Los Angeles Dodgers fans have seen a healthy and productive Shohei Ohtani in the lineup, but that wait could be nearly over.
Ohtani could be activated as soon as Wednesday, reports Sonja Chen of MLB.com.
That means Ohtani is likely to be playing in a couple of the games against the San Diego Padres in the last regular season home series of the season.
“There’s a good chance next series we’ll see him,” manager Dave Roberts said.
Why hasn’t Shohei Ohtani been playing?
Ohtani has been dealing with multiple injuries, including to his knee and his bicep.
Those injuries already shut down his pitching earlier this season, but even with a change to pitching-only duties, Ohtani was clearly suffering from something.
Ohtani had a four-hit game on Aug. 17, which included two home runs, and then his batting statistics fell off a cliff.
In the 14 games he’s played since that performance against the Colorado Rockies at Coors Field, Ohtani is hitting .130/.288/.241/.529, per Baseball Reference.
He has seven hits, including a double, a triple and a homer, but has also struck out 22 times.
Compare that to his overall season slash line of .277/.380/.522/.902, statistics that are much more in line with his reputation as one of the best baseball players of all time.
What will Shohei Ohtani be like when he returns to the Dodgers?
It’s worth noting that Ohtani, even with this 15-day stint on the injured list, won’t come back fully healed.
Chen said, though, that what was pain is now “discomfort.”
That sounds like Ohtani still won’t be 100%, but Ohtani at even 90% would be a perennial All-Star and could absolutely change the team’s fortunes in the playoffs.
We’ll know more for sure once Ohtani is back, as he’ll likely get a lot of playing time, Roberts said.
“If Ohtani returns when he is eligible on Wednesday, he will have only five regular-season games to reacclimate himself to big league action before the postseason,” Chen wrote. “Roberts said he plans to play Ohtani in every game once he returns because he will need the live at-bats.”
Once he does return, Roberts expects Ohtani to be much closer to his MVP form than he was for that rough stretch of August.
“I do think that when he’s activated,” Roberts said, “it’s going to be the best physical place he’s been in in quite some time.”
Do you think Shohei Ohtani will be back to playing like himself when he returns to the Dodgers this week?

item.title: [dodgersway.com] Dodgers map out Shohei Ohtani return with Roki Sasaki, Andy Pages roster moves
item.dc:creator: Jordan Campbell
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers are pacing toward having a first-round bye, avoiding the NL Wild Card round, and it would seem they are getting healthy at just the right time. The expectation in recent weeks was that Shohei Ohtani, Andy Pages, and Roki Sasaki would return before the end of the regular season, and the Dodgers quietly revealed the roster moves to map everything out. Updating their transaction log overnight, the Dodgers have reinstated Pages and Sasaki from the IL, and optioned Emmet Sheeh
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are pacing toward having a first-round bye, avoiding the NL Wild Card round, and it would seem they are getting healthy at just the right time. The expectation in recent weeks was that Shohei Ohtani, Andy Pages, and Roki Sasaki would return before the end of the regular season, and the Dodgers quietly revealed the roster moves to map everything out.
Updating their transaction log overnight, the Dodgers have reinstated Pages and Sasaki from the IL, and optioned Emmet Sheehan and Eliezer Alfonzo to the minors. With Ohtani eligible to be reinstated from the IL on Wednesday, the expectation is that Alex Freeland will be the corresponding move.
For Ohtani and Pages, the goal was simply having them back before the start of the playoffs. They now have a runway to shake off the rust over these next handful of games, before likely having next week off before playing in the NLDS.
Circumstances are a little more dire for Sasaki, who hasn't secured a spot on LA's playoff roster. Dave Roberts has already confirmed that Sasaki will be used out of the bullpen upon his return, and it goes to one of the biggest questions facing the Dodgers ahead of the playoffs.
The Dodgers are getting healthy just in time, but there are still answers needed
The Dodgers need to find answers in the bullpen. Ironically, the stage is set for Sasaki to repeat a similar shift he made last season. While the Dodgers have been adamant that Sasaki's future is as a starting pitcher, he was used as a quasi-finisher during the playoffs last year, and thrived.
Considering the questions surrounding Edwin Diaz and Edgardo Henriquez currently dealing with an injury, Sasaki once again becoming an effective high-leverage option for the Dodgers would be a major development for the playoffs.
The story of the Dodgers since the trade deadline has been that they are leaking oil. Sure, they traded for Tarik Skubal, but the operation looked faulty. With the returns of Sasaki, Pages, and Ohtani likely on Wednesday, they are finally reaching a level of healthy they haven't had for most of the season.
In other words, despite how uneven things have looked, the Dodgers are once again in a position to do whay they do best and flip the swith on during the month of October.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] The latest on MLB postseason clinches, Shohei Ohtani and Aaron Judge health updates, awards races, and more
item.dc:creator: Associated Press
item.description: Major League Baseball's postseason rapidly is approaching, with the Los Angeles Dodgers seeking a third straight World Series title. It remains to be seen how much some of the game's biggest stars will be able to participate in the playoffs, though. The Dodgers are once again among the best teams in the big leagues, and they'll have several challengers in October, including the Milwaukee Brewers and Tampa Bay Rays. All three teams could finish the regular season with 100 wins or more. Los Angele
item.content:encoded:
Major League Baseball's postseason rapidly is approaching, with the Los Angeles Dodgers seeking a third straight World Series title. It remains to be seen how much some of the game's biggest stars will be able to participate in the playoffs, though.
The Dodgers are once again among the best teams in the big leagues, and they'll have several challengers in October, including the Milwaukee Brewers and Tampa Bay Rays. All three teams could finish the regular season with 100 wins or more. Los Angeles is rolling even though four-time MVP Shohei Ohtani's health is a concern.
The New York Yankees, Boston Red Sox and Atlanta Braves also have clinched spots in the postseason. Yankees slugger Aaron Judge, a three-time AL MVP, is dealing with a right calf strain that will keep him on the injured list until at least the final day of the regular season.
While the 12-team playoff field appears mostly set, there are a few long-shot contenders for the postseason, and specific matchups are in flux.
Here's some of what to watch as the season comes to a close.
AL race is murky while NL is more defined
There's quite a bit of mediocrity in the AL Central and West divisions this season, which has led to some fascinating pennant races and could lead to a sub-.500 team making the postseason.
The Cleveland Guardians (81-75) have a narrow advantage over the Chicago White Sox (80-76) in the AL Central while the Texas Rangers (78-78) are just ahead of the Houston Astros (77-79) in the AL West.
Over in the National League, the playoff bracket is close to set.
The Chicago Cubs (87-69), San Diego Padres (87-69) and Philadelphia Phillies (86-70) are jockeying for position in the wild-card race but almost certainly will make the postseason. The only team within shouting distance is the Arizona Diamondbacks (82-74), who are four games back.
MVP races, stats to watch
MLB's major awards probably won't have much drama this season.
Both MVP races have strong favorites with Chicago's Pete Crow-Armstrong running away with the NL honor while Houston's Yordan Alvarez is the probable choice in the AL, though Tampa Bay's Junior Caminero also has had a fantastic season. Alvarez still has a shot at a rare Triple Crown. He leads the AL in batting average at .313 but his 40 homers are one behind Caminero and his 99 RBIs are nine back of Baltimore's Pete Alonso.
For the Cy Young Award, Milwaukee flame thrower Jacob Misiorowski and New York ace Cam Schlittler are the favorites in the NL and AL, respectively.
The Rookie of the Year races also look set with Cincinnati's Sal Stewart and his 110-RBI season the leader in the NL and Detroit's Kevin McGonigle the favorite in the AL.
What is the MLB playoff format?
There are 12 teams that qualify for MLB's postseason, including six teams from both the AL and NL. The three division winners in each league get seeds No. 1 through No. 3, ranked by win-loss record. Then the three wild-card teams get seeds No. 4 through No. 6, also ranked by win-loss record.
The top two teams with the best record in both the AL and NL automatically advance to the Division Series. The other eight teams play in the Wild Card Series, which is a best-of-three format beginning on Tuesday, Sept. 30. In both the AL and NL, the No. 6 seed will travel to face the No. 3 seed while the No. 5 seed goes to No. 4. The higher seed hosts all three games.
The winners then advance to the best-of-five Division Series, followed by the best-of-seven League Championship Series and a best-of-seven World Series between the winners of the AL and NL.
What is the MLB postseason schedule?
Wild Card Round: Sept. 29-Oct. 1 (NBC/Peacock)
Division Series: Oct. 3-10 (AL on TBS, NL on FOX/FS1)
Championship Series: Oct. 11-20 (AL on TBS, NL on FOX/FS1)
World Series: Oct. 23-31 (FOX)
Who are the favorites to win the World Series?
The Dodgers (+220) are the favorites to capture a third straight World Series title while the Brewers (+600), Yankees (+800) and Rays (+800) are viewed as the top contenders.

item.title: [Los Angeles Times] The Dodgers’ Josue De Paula can hit. Now he’s out to prove he can play defense, too
item.dc:creator: Maddie Lee
item.description: - Click here to listen to this article - Dodgers rookie Josue De Paula sat down with third base and outfield coach Dino Ebel in the visiting coach’s room at Great American Ball Park. Ebel pulled up defensive metrics on three different outfielders. One was Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong, the National League MVP favorite and MLB’s defensive fWAR leader. Another was Dodgers center fielder Andy Pages, who has evolved into an elite center fielder during his time with the organization.
item.content:encoded:
- Click here to listen to this article
-
Dodgers rookie Josue De Paula sat down with third base and outfield coach Dino Ebel in the visiting coach’s room at Great American Ball Park. Ebel pulled up defensive metrics on three different outfielders.
One was Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong, the National League MVP favorite and MLB’s defensive fWAR leader. Another was Dodgers center fielder Andy Pages, who has evolved into an elite center fielder during his time with the organization. And the third was De Paula.
“There’s a lot of colors in the game, and when you have red, it’s not good, and when you have green, it’s good,” Ebel said in a recent conversation with The Times. “And he saw a lot of green from the other two players, and he saw some green and some red on his side. So it kind of hit home with him.”
The reports broke down his first step, going right and left, arm strength, and so on.
For the past 17 years, Chaz Perea and his four-person crew have been responsible for every bit of stadium landscaping that isn’t the field itself.
“Just comparing [Pages’] journey, too, with mine — and that it’s possible,” De Paula said of what he took from the conversation. “I have all the tools under my belt to be able to do so. It’s more about just being focused throughout the whole thing, and having that drive to want to do it.
“And when I saw it, it was also a motivation for me. It was like, all right, let’s go now.”
It was De Paula’s bat that earned him a call-up when Shohei Ohtani landed on the injured list. And it’s his bat that’s now making his case for a postseason roster spot. (“This is more of a trial run,” manager Dave Roberts said last week.)
For De Paula to stick in the majors, however, his development on the defensive side is going to be key. As he has risen through the system, his outfield play has lagged behind his offensive influence. But the Dodgers have already seen growth this year.
“Our goal is to become, one day, a Gold Glover,” Ebel said. “And I think he’s young enough to do it, and his mindset is right, he’s got a chance to do that.”
Dodgers special assistant Jason Heyward started poring over video of the team’s top prospects — a group chalk full of outfielders, led by De Paula — as soon as he began working for the Dodgers’ front office at the beginning of May.
“He handles constructive criticism, for me, with some of the best of them that I’ve been around,” Heyward said.
Heyward, a five-time Gold Glove outfielder, first met De Paula in spring training in 2024, when the prospect jumped in on outfield drills with the major leaguers. In Heyward’s new role, he’s made multiple trips to Tulsa, Okla., to work with De Paula and the rest of the group there.
Heyward emphasized building a consistent and productive routine.
“He makes it so easy to have something to make relatable to this because I’ve seen his work in the cage, I’ve seen his attention to detail,” Heyward said. “He takes on challenges, but it’s not a, ‘Let me hurry up and get to this challenge, let me rush through this.’ He’s like, ‘No, I’m going to go about this how I want to go about it, I’m not going to be rushed, I’m going to lock in, and I’m going to give this like all my focus.’”
That process on the offensive side was something Heyward encouraged De Paula to tap into in all parts of his game, including defense. But De Paula said Heyward also acknowledged that the nature of playing in the outfield can make that more difficult.
“Hitting, you are always unfocused on the next pitch, your mind is always going,” De Paula said. “But you could go three days without getting a fly ball. So it’s kind of easy for your mind to drift and stuff like that. But it’s just more about tips of engagement and that intensity of focus.”
Heyward was a fitting person to deliver the message. Once a heralded prospect for the Braves, he put together a 16-year MLB career that included a second-place rookie of the year finish, an All-Star nod, and a stellar reputation for defense and veteran leadership.
“It’s a blessing to have somebody like that in your corner, especially rooting for you, to be able to see your talent, like what you’re capable of,” De Paula said. “He’s been through it, so he knows, man. So it’s awesome to have somebody like that as your mentor.”
Coincidentally, De Paula would go on to launch a three-run home run as his first major-league hit, a feat he shares with Heyward — although Heyward did it in his first at-bat.
“It’s a very commendable job that all of our staff have done at every level,” Heyward said. “... I’d be doing a big injustice without giving everyone their flowers on this because it’s definitely been a group effort. … For someone like him who became a part of the organization at 16 years old, he’s a Dodger through and through.”
Over the past week and a half, the major-league coaching staff, which also had De Paula in major-league spring training camp the last two years, has taken over. And already, they’ve seen the benefit of the routine he’s developed this year.
“All the reports that we’ve gotten from our minor-league staff are right on cue,” Ebel said. “He’s been working, he’s bringing it right here to the major leagues. And it’s a pleasure for me, with some energy, coming out early every day — hasn’t missed. We’re working on game situations, ground balls, left, right, right at him, fly balls, shags during BP. So we’re on the right track.”
Dodgers two-time Cy Young winner Blake Snell joined them one day in Miami, catching De Paula’s throws in early work. Though the new teammates wanted to keep the specifics of their conversations between them, Snell’s advice and encouragement made an impression — “It’s like putting fuel in a rocket,” De Paula said.
“He’s just really, really talented, lots to learn,” Snell said. “And excited for him in his journey and what it could turn into.”
In the next city, Cincinnati, Roberts spent an afternoon in left field with him while he was shagging fly balls during batting practice.
“I wanted to be up close to watch him get off on the baseball, watch his reads, his angles to balls and make sure he’s shagging the right way,” Roberts said. “Had some instruction for him; he was great.”
Mookie Betts hits three doubles and the Dodgers piled up 15 hits in a 10-4 win over the San Francisco Giants with Shohei Ohtani’s return on the horizon.
Roberts, too, has challenged De Paula to make defense a strength, one that will keep him in games, rather than lifted for a defensive replacement. And De Paula has met it with bright eyes and motivation.
“The trust on the defense is going to come,” De Paula said. “I have to prove it over time. And with the work that I’m doing on the field, I know I’m going to gain it.”
A gold glove is a goal of his too.
“That’s one thing about me, when my mind is set on something, I feel like it’s no going back,” De Paula said. “So, I’ve gotten a lot of hate on my defense, and I just love to prove people wrong. So I’m like, hey, all right, there’s a weakness there, but I’m gonna shut you up. Just give me some time. I’ve got you.”

item.title: [DodgersBeat] Shohei Ohtani Featured in MLB Kids Stop-Motion Series
item.dc:creator: Los Royers
item.description: LOS ANGELES, CA — Shohei Ohtani and the Los Angeles Dodgers will take center stage in the next episode of MLB Clubhouse’s stop-motion series, “The Doug Out!,” scheduled to premiere Tuesday, September 22, at 8:30 a.m. ET on the MLB Clubhouse YouTube channel. item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES, CA — Shohei Ohtani and the Los Angeles Dodgers will take center stage in the next episode of MLB Clubhouse’s stop-motion series, “The Doug Out!,” scheduled to premiere Tuesday, September 22, at 8:30 a.m. ET on the MLB Clubhouse YouTube channel.
The kid-focused episode presents Ohtani as a baseball superstar whose rare combination of pitching, power hitting and speed makes him one of the sport’s most compelling players. It uses humor, animation and simple explanations to introduce younger viewers to his two-way role.
How the episode introduces Shohei Ohtani
The episode follows host Doug as he tries to match Ohtani’s preparation by taking a series of exaggerated power naps. That running joke leads into a “superstar snapshot” covering Ohtani’s work as a starting pitcher and hitter, along with his home-run power, velocity and speed on the bases.
The story also brings in several parts of Ohtani’s life and Dodgers identity that young fans will recognize. His dog, Decoy, appears in the conversation, while Mookie Betts is highlighted as a teammate and fan favorite.
A separate sketchbook segment explains how a grand slam works by showing the bases loaded and all four runners scoring on one home run. The episode then moves into Dodgers trivia, touching on Dodger Stadium, the franchise’s history and the team’s familiar on-base celebration.
MLB Clubhouse targets baseball’s next generation
“The Doug Out!” is in its inaugural season as a season-long stop-motion series on MLB Clubhouse, a YouTube channel created to help children learn about baseball, its clubs and its biggest personalities.
The Ohtani installment continues MLB’s broader effort to make the sport more accessible to younger audiences through short-form, family-friendly programming. More information about the channel and its programming is available in MLB’s original MLB Clubhouse announcement.
The episode is scheduled to premiere on the MLB Clubhouse YouTube channel Tuesday at 8:30 a.m. ET.
More Dodgers Coverage:
Have you subscribed to the Bleed Los Podcast YouTube channel? Be sure to ring the notification bell to watch player interviews, participate in shows & promotions, and stay up to date on all Dodgers news and rumors!

item.title: [whittierdailynews.com] Are the Dodgers finding the best version of themselves just in time?
item.dc:creator: Doug Padilla

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — The energy emanating from the steamroller heading up I-5 on Monday radiated for miles.
Fuel was used to power the buses the San Diego Padres used to make the trip north for a three-game series that starts Tuesday night, but only because they didn’t try adrenaline.
Winners in 13 of their past 14 games, the Padres are poised to accomplish team history over the next few days. Never in their existence have they made the playoffs in three consecutive seasons.
San Diego has a magic number of two to clinch a National League wild-card spot, although the Padres intend to run through the finish line with a chance at ascending to the top of the wild-card heap in the NL.
“I feel like the whole team is in a good spot right now,” San Diego’s Fernando Tatis Jr. told the San Diego Union-Tribune on Sunday. “We’re playing really good baseball. We’re checking in when we have to. The entire lineup is in a good spot right now. So when it’s going like that, it’s … a good time.”
The Dodgers already have another NL West title secured (their 13th in the past 14 years), but they also have a magic number of three to clinch a top-two seed in the NL playoffs and a bye into one of the best-of-five Division Series.
“I think it’s going to be a good kind of (playoff) primer,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said of the upcoming series. “They’re a very talented team. They’re playing as good as anyone in all of baseball. I’m looking forward to playing those guys and just kind of ramping it up a little bit more for our guys.”
With the Dodgers on a 14-3 run since Sept. 3, they are on a familiar final month charge toward the playoffs. Second-half lulls in each of the past two seasons have transformed into Septembers when the group has discovered the best version of itself.
Last season, the Dodgers were swept in a three-game series by the Angels in August then opened September with a three-game dud in Pittsburgh. A disastrous loss in Baltimore lit the fire after Yoshinobu Yamamoto lost a no-hitter with two outs in the ninth inning and the Dodgers never recorded another out while losing the game.
The wide-awake Dodgers went 15-5 the rest of the way, stormed through the NL playoffs – going 9-1 against the Cincinnati Reds, Philadelphia Phillies and Milwaukee Brewers – then came out on top in a dramatic seven-game World Series against the Toronto Blue Jays.
Earlier this month, it was a brutal 8-6 loss in 10 innings to the St. Louis Cardinals on Sept. 2 that was the wake-up call. It included a four-strikeout night from Shohei Ohtani, who played just one more game before taking his current spot on the injured list.
Properly motivated, the Dodgers have gone on a tear ever since, but it has come at the expense of teams that were not in playoff contention like the Washington Nationals, Reds, Miami Marlins and San Francisco Giants.
This week marks the Dodgers’ first chance to face a team playing at the peak of its powers since they faced the Boston Red Sox, Chicago Cubs, Milwaukee Brewers and Atlanta Braves all in a recent 25-game stretch. They flubbed that test by going 1-12 in those games.
Mookie Betts, Kyle Tucker and Will Smith all have put a charge into the resurgence, while the arrival of rookie Josue De Paula has given the lineup another hitter who can extend at-bats with a discerning eye, along with Max Muncy.
Betts went 0 for 4 in Sunday’s 3-1 victory over the Giants, yet he still is hitting .373 with six home runs, 20 RBIs and a 1.215 OPS in 17 games since the start of September.
Far from content with an offense that has averaged 5.8 runs per game this month, Betts said the Dodgers can do even more. After all, Andy Pages is set to return Tuesday, while Ohtani could be back later this week.
“Some guys are hitting, some guys are not,” Betts said. “I think that’s the beauty of the lineup. You get a couple guys going, and a couple guys here can carry a team, and you never know. You just never know who’s it going to be, it’s different guys every day.”
Amid a brutal first season with the Dodgers, Tucker has done his part lately by going 15 for 36 (.417) over his past 11 games with five home runs and 11 RBIs. He was limited to coming off the bench on Sunday after he fouled a ball off his right knee on Saturday.
Tucker was not with the club for last year’s September revival, but he has helped power this one. When it comes to team potential, Tucker is a big-picture guy.
“I think our potential is winning the World Series,” Tucker said. “So (when) we do that, then I can say we reached it. But we feel like we’re in a good spot right now. Our pitching staff’s done a great job all year giving us an opportunity to win every single night. Our defense has played pretty well behind them and then offensively we’ve done a solid job as well.”
“Right now, we got a few guys that are feeling good. A few guys that are banged up. But we’re still out there grinding trying to win as many games as possible before the season ends and just trying to carry it all the way to the playoffs.”
At the very least, confidence will be high this week, in both dugouts.
UP NEXT
Padres (RHP Michael King, 12-9, 3.03 ERA) at Dodgers (TBA), Tuesday, 7:10 p.m., SportsNet LA, 570 AM

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] MLB Injury Report: Dodgers to get Shohei Ohtani, Andy Pages, and Roki Sasaki back for postseason run
item.dc:creator: Jorge Montanez
item.description: In this week's Injury Report, the Dodgers are getting a number of key players back this week as they prepare for another deep playoff run in their quest to three-peat. Alex Bregman hopes to return sometime in the postseason after suffering multiple facial fractures in a terrible, freak accident on the on-deck circle. And Dylan Cease has likely made his last start after experiencing shoulder fatigue. That and more in the final week's injury report. ⚾️ Baseball is back! MLB returns to NBC and Peac
item.content:encoded:
In this week's Injury Report, the Dodgers are getting a number of key players back this week as they prepare for another deep playoff run in their quest to three-peat. Alex Bregman hopes to return sometime in the postseason after suffering multiple facial fractures in a terrible, freak accident on the on-deck circle. And Dylan Cease has likely made his last start after experiencing shoulder fatigue. That and more in the final week's injury report.
⚾️ Baseball is back! MLB returns to NBC and Peacock in 2026! In addition to becoming the exclusive home of Sunday Night Baseball, NBC Sports will broadcast MLB Sunday Leadoff, "Opening Day" and Labor Day primetime games, the first round of the MLB Draft, the entire Wild Card round of the postseason, and much more.
Shohei Ohtani (knee, biceps)
Andy Pages (hand)
Blake Snell (groin)
Roki Sasaki (blister)
Ohtani has been out of action for the last two weeks, sidelined with lingering knee and biceps injuries. Manager Dave Roberts told reporters on Sunday that the 32-year-old star should be expected to return from the injured list and join the Dodgers lineup on Wednesday. Ohtani should be in the lineup for the remaining games to get some needed at-bats before the postseason. The team also gets Pages back this week, activating him from the injured list ahead of Tuesday's series opener against the Padres. He's been out for a month with a left hand fracture. The two additions this week are obviously a significant boost for a Dodgers team looking to three-peat. Their returns likely shift rookie Josue De Paula to a reserve or utility role.
On the pitching side, Snell left his start last Wednesday against the Reds with left groin tightness. He stated the issue was not serious and plans on making one more start before the postseason. That start isn't going to come when his spot in the rotation comes up on Tuesday, but the plan is for him to pitch over the weekend, according to Roberts.
From Yordan Alvarez to Zack Wheeler, an A-to-Z look at the players, performances, and trends that defined the 2026 MLB regular season.
Alex Bregman (face)
Bregman was struck by a foul ball while on the on-deck circle on Sunday against the Reds and was sent to the hospital, where he was diagnosed with multiple facial fractures. The freak accident is an unfortunate development this late in the season as the Cubs prepare to enter the playoffs. The team is hoping to get their 32-year-old star third baseman back at some point in the postseason, and it is a relief that the injury didn't result in anything more serious. Meanwhile, Sasaki was activated on Monday after missing some time with a blister issue and will pitch as a one-inning reliever, auditioning for a spot in the Dodgers bullpen in the postseason.
Dylan Cease (shoulder)
Cease has likely made his final start of the season. The 30-year-old right-hander underwent an MRI on his right shoulder over the weekend after experiencing some fatigue. The imaging revealed some shoulder inflammation, but no structural damage that would require surgery, and nothing that would bring into question his availability for next season. With the Blue Jays 3.5 games out of a Wild Card spot, it doesn't make much sense for Cease to push for one more start over the final weekend. If his season is indeed over, he'll end the year with a strong 2.40 ERA, 1.10 WHIP, and 239 strikeouts over 169 innings.
Andrés Muñoz (knee)
Muñoz left Sunday's game against the Rockies with a knee injury after giving up a home run and a walk. He was set to undergo an MRI on his right knee, the results of which are still unknown. The 27-year-old right-hander had a tough, disappointing season, posting a 4.24 ERA, 1.22 WHIP, and 89 strikeouts over 57 1/3 innings while converting 28 of 38 save chances. If he's unable to pitch over the final week, it could be Seranthony Domíguez closing out the remaining games.
Bryce Eldridge (concussion)
More Giants injuries that seemingly come out of nowhere. Eldridge was scratched from Friday's lineup against the Dodgers due to a head laceration after bumping his head on a low-hanging ceiling at the team hotel. He still "felt woozy" throughout the weekend and entered the concussion protocol before the team ultimately placed him on the 7-day concussion injured list. The move is retroactive to Friday, so there's a chance he could return for the final weekend series, though that's probably unlikely. The 21-year-old slugger flashed immense potential this season, hitting .269/.364/.461 with 17 homers and 57 RBI across 448 plate appearances.
Colt Keith (thumb)
Keith's season is over after the team placed him on the 10-day injured list with a left thumb sprain. It's an issue that the 25-year-old infielder has been playing through over the last several weeks. He ends the season hitting a modest .258/.322/.406 with 10 homers, 51 runs scored, 36 RBI, and six steals across 423 plate appearances.

item.title: [New York Post] Dodgers’ plan for Shohei Ohtani is unnecessarily risky
item.dc:creator: Dylan Hernandez
item.description: The Dodgers have lost this gamble once before. But that won’t stop them from placing the same wager again. Rather than take every precaution to ensure Shohei Ohtani doesn’t worsen the injuries to his right arm and left knee, the Dodgers will prioritize giving him at-bats to get him ready for the playoffs. Ohtani is expected to be activated from the 15-day injured list Wednesday, and manager Dave Roberts said the plan is for him to play in every one of the five games that remain in the regular se
item.content:encoded:
The Dodgers have lost this gamble once before. But that won’t stop them from placing the same wager again.
Rather than take every precaution to ensure Shohei Ohtani doesn’t worsen the injuries to his right arm and left knee, the Dodgers will prioritize giving him at-bats to get him ready for the playoffs.
Ohtani is expected to be activated from the 15-day injured list Wednesday, and manager Dave Roberts said the plan is for him to play in every one of the five games that remain in the regular season.
“He’ll need those live at-bats,” Roberts said.
This feels reckless — and unnecessarily risky, especially when considering what happened the last time the Dodgers were in this position, just earlier this month.
Ohtani was experiencing discomfort in his arm and knee. The Dodgers downplayed the severity of his injuries, with general manager Brandon Gomes claiming the physical problems weren’t responsible for his hitting slump and shouldn’t require him to be placed on the IL.
So much for that.
Roberts described Ohtani as being “pain-free” Sunday, but acknowledged he was still experiencing “discomfort you can play through.” Certain levels of discomfort can be tolerated — until they can’t be, of course. That’s been the story of Ohtani’s season.
When Ohtani started feeling pain in his knee, he insisted he could pitch through it. Until he couldn’t.
When he started to be affected in the batter’s box by the throbbing in his arm and knee, he claimed he could play it. Until he couldn’t.
Roberts said Ohtani’s condition has improved over the last two weeks. But Roberts also didn’t claim Ohtani was completely healthy.
“Is he 100%?” Roberts said. “Probably not.”
In other words, what bothered Ohtani when he landed on the IL still bothers him, just not as much.
This is a problem.
What happened earlier this month showed that if Ohtani plays too many games with these particular injuries, he will reach a point where he won’t even be able to take the field.
Why not give Ohtani every other game off? Will playing five more regular-season games instead of three make that much of a difference? Because the question isn’t whether Ohtani can make it through the next five games. The question is how much closer these games will push him to the point of no return.
The objective should be to make sure Ohtani is available in some capacity throughout the entire postseason, not only at the start of it. If he has to be gradually work his way into form over the playoffs, so be it.
Ohtani would almost certainly reject such cautious thinking. He doesn’t like half-measures. Ohtani takes big swings without much regard to the consequences.
So, if he’s going to use the final week of the regular season to prepare for the playoffs, he’ll probably do so with visions of being an impact player. He doesn’t want a Kirk Gibson moment; he wants to be Mr. October.
Before he went on the IL, Ohtani offered a realistic assessment of his health, saying he didn’t expect to be at 100% between now and the end of the season. But he said he believed he could overcome his physical problems by making adjustments to his swing.
“With some creativity, I think I can make up for what’s not right,” Ohtani said in Japanese. “Another way to say it is that it’s an opportunity to create new ways to compete.”
At the time, that meant learning how to hit with one arm and one leg.
The Dodgers let him, and Ohtani ended up on the IL.
Once again, it sounds as if Ohtani is determined to squeeze in as many at-bats as possible, and once again, it sounds as if the Dodgers will let him try.
This approach has significant upside — and downside, too.

item.title: [windfm.com] Justin Verlander is retiring. With a work stoppage on the horizon, how many others might join him? - WINDFM - 92.5 Gainesville 95.5 Ocala
item.dc:creator: Schristian
item.description: By NOAH TRISTER AP Baseball Writer Justin Verlander and Max Scherzer were together on some memorable Detroit teams before moving on and winning championships elsewhere. Will they eventually enter the Hall of Fame as part of the same class? The first question is whether both will retire after this season. The 43-year-old Verlander has already announced this is his final year. He’s made only one start in a reunion season with the Tigers, although Detroit fans are hoping he can return for another t
item.content:encoded:
By NOAH TRISTER AP Baseball Writer
Justin Verlander and Max Scherzer were together on some memorable Detroit teams before moving on and winning championships elsewhere.
Will they eventually enter the Hall of Fame as part of the same class?
The first question is whether both will retire after this season. The 43-year-old Verlander has already announced this is his final year. He’s made only one start in a reunion season with the Tigers, although Detroit fans are hoping he can return for another this coming week.
Scherzer’s future is less clear. The 42-year-old right-hander is slated to start Tuesday at Baltimore as the Blue Jays try to keep their flickering playoff hopes alive, but Scherzer has posted ERAs over 5.00 both this season and last. He’s on a one-year contract with Toronto.
Some other prominent players may also have made — or might be making — their last appearances in the major leagues. Trey Mancini signed a one-day contract to retire with the Orioles and was celebrated this past weekend in Baltimore. Andrew McCutchen and Carlos Santana, both 39, were released last month. Craig Kimbrel, now 38, has pitched for 10 different big league teams in the last six seasons.
Paul Goldschmidt is 39, but his team — the New York Yankees — is heading to the playoffs. And he may be more important than expected if Aaron Judge is out.
With a lockout possible after this season, there could be some retirements we don’t anticipate. Rick Sutcliffe, Bo Jackson and Hall of Famer Goose Gossage, for example, never played again after the 1994 strike but didn’t actually retire until the following year.
Trivia time
Who is the most recent player voted into the Hall of Fame by the BBWAA whose primary team was the Tigers? (The drought is likely to end soon with Miguel Cabrera and then Verlander.)
Performance of the week
Angel Martínez homered from both sides of the plate and had four hits in Cleveland’s 12-6 win over the Athletics on Saturday night. The Guardians have won five straight and are closing in on a postseason spot. They have a one-game lead over the Chicago White Sox atop the AL Central, and it’s another three games back from the White Sox to Toronto and Houston in the race for the last wild card.
In the National League, Philadelphia leads Arizona by four games for the final wild card, so anyone rooting for chaos this coming week may be disappointed.
Comeback of the week
Detroit was down 8-2 in the fifth inning Friday night before scoring nine unanswered runs to win 11-8 over the White Sox. Kevin McGonigle hit a three-run triple, and both Hao-Yu Lee and Riley Greene added two-run homers during the comeback. Detroit’s win probability was down to 3.2% in the fourth inning according to Baseball Savant.
That’s the only game the Tigers have won out of their last five. They’ve been eliminated from the playoff race, the end of a frustrating season in which nothing seemed to go as planned.
Team of the week
The Los Angeles Dodgers and San Diego Padres both went 6-1, with the Dodgers posting the superior run differential. A three-game sweep of San Francisco leaves the Dodgers four games ahead of Atlanta for the second bye in the National League as they try for a third consecutive World Series title.
There are still health concerns for the Dodgers, with Shohei Ohtani on the injured list and Blake Snell having left his last start after one inning.
Los Angeles did get Edwin Diaz back, and he threw scoreless innings on back-to-back days Friday and Saturday.
Trivia answer
Al Kaline, who was inducted in 1980.
George Kell, Hal Newhouser, Jim Bunning, Sparky Anderson, Jack Morris and Alan Trammell have been elected since then with the Tigers as their primary team, but they weren’t voted in by the BBWAA.
___

item.content:encoded:
- MLB. Wyatt Langford salta sobre el catcher de Toronto en una espectacular jugada de los Rangers
- MLB. Aaron Judge desata la preocupación tras abandonar el juego por una lesión repentina días después de volver a MLB
Existe cierta preocupación entre los aficionados sobre cuánto tiempo necesitará Shohei Ohtani para recuperarse antes de volver finalmente con los Los Angeles Dodgers, quienes ya aseguraron su boleto a los playoffs y buscan disputar su tercera Serie Mundial consecutiva.
Afortunadamente para los Dodgers, el regreso de la estrella japonesa está cada vez más cerca después de dar otro paso positivo en su recuperación ofensiva, por lo que podría volver tan pronto como el inicio de la próxima serie ante los San Diego Padres.
¿Qué dijo Dave Roberts sobre Shohei Ohtani?
El manager Dave Roberts confirmó que Ohtani (molestias en el bíceps derecho y la rodilla izquierda) continúa con una evolución favorable y está cada vez más cerca de regresar a la acción. El japonés podría ser activado de la lista de lesionados de 15 días durante la próxima serie de Los Ángeles.
“Hay una buena posibilidad de que lo veamos en la próxima serie”, aseguró Roberts después de la victoria de los Dodgers por 10-4 sobre los Giants en el Dodger Stadium.
Ohtani fue colocado en la lista de lesionados con fecha retroactiva al 8 de septiembre, por lo que sería elegible para regresar el miércoles, en el segundo partido de la última serie de temporada regular como local ante los San Diego Padres. Su regreso será únicamente como bateador, ya que los Dodgers decidieron detener por ahora su actividad como lanzador.
El astro japonés ya comenzó a recuperar ritmo en la caja de bateo. Después de iniciar su programa de progresión ofensiva el martes, Ohtani dio el siguiente paso al enfrentar lanzamientos de la máquina Trajekt, un dispositivo que simula enfrentar a pitchers reales.
De acuerdo con Roberts, el japonés terminó con buenas sensaciones después de realizar entre 30 y 40 swings el sábado, además de trabajar en el corrido de bases durante la práctica de bateo.
Una recuperación fugaz antes de los playoffs
Si Ohtani regresa el miércoles, cuando sea elegible para salir de la lista de lesionados, solamente tendrá cinco partidos de temporada regular para recuperar ritmo, encontrar nuevamente su timing en el plato y adaptarse a la intensidad de las Grandes Ligas antes del inicio de la postemporada.
Por ello, Dave Roberts planea colocarlo en la alineación en todos los encuentros disponibles, ya que el japonés necesita acumular turnos reales al bate para recuperar confianza y llegar en mejores condiciones al momento más importante del año.
Ohtani tampoco tendrá una asignación de rehabilitación en Ligas Menores, debido a que la temporada regular de Triple-A termina el domingo y los Dodgers no cuentan con pitchers adicionales disponibles para realizar sesiones de bateo en vivo.

item.title: [日刊スポーツ] ESPNがポストシーズンの先発ローテランキング掲載 山本由伸、スクバルらのドジャース１位 - ＭＬＢ : 日刊スポーツ
item.description: ESPNは21日（日本時間22日）、ポストシーズンに出場する可能性がある15チームの先発ローテランキングを掲載し、山本由伸投手（27）らを擁するドジャースが1位に選ばれた。 ドジャースの先発陣は山本に加えてスクバル、スネル、グラスノーらで形成され、同メディアは「ドジャースはこの部門で依然としてトップ。現在離脱している大谷翔平が今シーズン中に再び登板する可能性は低いとはいえ、かなりの差がある。以下に挙げる5、6チームのどの投手よりも優れている投手4人を7試合制のシリーズで先発させることができる」と記した。 2位は現在ナ・リーグ勝率1位で、剛腕ミジオロウスキーらを擁するブルワーズ。3位にはフィリーズが入った。日本選手の所属チームでは、吉田正尚のレッドソックスが5位、岡本和真のブルージェイズが6位、今井達也のアストロズが12位、鈴木誠也と今永昇太のカブスが13位、ダルビッシュ有と松井裕樹のパドレスが14位、村上宗隆のホワイトソックスが15位となっている。

item.title: [marinij.com] Wilkinson’s impressive five shutout innings can’t prevent SF Giants from being swept by Dodgers
item.dc:creator: Justice delos Santos
item.description: LOS ANGELES — Matt Wilkinson’s role has been nebulous during his short time in the majors. In his debut, he was an opener. On some days, he’s made traditional starts. In others, he’s been a multi-inning reliever. Wilkinson is one of several young, inexperienced pitchers on this roster trying to prove he can start at the major-league level. item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — Matt Wilkinson’s role has been nebulous during his short time in the majors. In his debut, he was an opener. On some days, he’s made traditional starts. In others, he’s been a multi-inning reliever.
Wilkinson is one of several young, inexperienced pitchers on this roster trying to prove he can start at the major-league level. His performance on Sunday afternoon at Dodger Stadium helped those efforts.
“Tugboat” couldn’t prevent the Giants, who lost 3-1 to the Dodgers, from being swept, but the rookie turned in arguably the best start of his short career. In his seventh career appearance, Wilkinson tossed five shutout innings against the NL West champions, collecting a career-high six strikeouts without recording a single walk.
“He was outstanding,” said manager Tony Vitello. “Back at it on the starting deal. To be honest with you, didn’t have a whole lot of trouble to navigate because of how well he threw the ball. … When there was potential for things brewing, he put an end to it.”
“Best one yet since being up,” Wilkinson said. “Really was just throwing all four pitches for strikes today, and that was kind of the mindset going into today. Compete with all four pitches, and I felt like I did a good job with that today.”
Vitello said it’s “too early” to know how Wilkinson could fit into next year’s pitching plans but assessed that Wilkinson is “pretty flexible.” Before Sunday, Wilkinson had pitched five scoreless innings with four strikeouts over his last two outings as a multi-inning reliever. When asked if he prefers starting or relieving, the 23-year-old responded he’s willing to pitch whatever role is needed.
“You want a guy that wants the ball and ain’t scared of those situations,” Vitello said.
Wilkinson certainly didn’t look scared in his first meeting with the reigning back-to-back World Series champions on their home turf. Even with Shohei Ohtani on the injured list and Kyle Tucker starting the day on the bench, the Dodgers’ lineup still featured future Hall of Famers Mookie Betts and Freddie Freeman and multi-time All-Stars Max Muncy and Teoscar Hernández.
Against Wilkinson, that group couldn’t get anything cooking.
The only threats that the Dodgers posed against Wilkinson were one-out doubles in the second and fifth innings. On both occasions, Wilkinson maneuvered out of trouble and completed five innings for just the second time in his career.
“Especially with this rivalry, it’s awesome and fun to be a small piece of that,” Wilkinson said.
Despite Wilkinson’s efforts, the Dodgers generated enough offense after his departure to complete the dusting.
Tommy Edman tied the game in the bottom of the sixth by turning a 2-2 cutter from Carson Seymour into a solo homer, and Kiké Hernández drove in the go-ahead run in the bottom of the seventh. Muncy, a long-time Giants (64-92) foe, added an RBI single in the bottom of the eighth for insurance.
Jonah Cox, with the use of his elite speed, generated San Francisco’s lone run in the top of the first.
Cox began the afternoon with a leadoff walk, then scrambled to second when the Dodgers’ Jack Dreyer made an errant pickoff throw. Already in scoring position, Cox swiped third with ease, his 14th steal of the season, then scored on a single by Victor Bericoto.
Following Dreyer’s lone inning as the opener, San Francisco couldn’t generate any offense against Los Angeles’ Emmet Sheehan, who allowed one hit over 5 1/3 scoreless innings of long relief with nine strikeouts. Sheehan has been outstanding against the Giants in his career, allowing four runs over 33 1/3 innings
By afternoon’s end, the Giants were reduced to their most inexperienced, anonymous lineup of the season. Rookie Bryce Eldridge missed a third straight game due to a head laceration, and right fielder Jung Hoo Lee was lifted from the game after fouling a pitch off his groin in the top of the sixth. Eldridge is not expected to play on Monday.
Up next
The Giants will return to Oracle Park for their final six games of the regular season, beginning with a three-game set against the Minnesota Twins.

item.title: [fantasy.fangraphs.com] FAAB Frenzy and Waivers Wild: Week 27
item.dc:creator: Vlad Sedler

item.content:encoded:
Every Monday, this column will break down the most popular waiver wire and free agent acquisitions from the weekend. I dig into the top adds on the ever-popular Fantrax and in the NFBC Online Championship (OC), a national mid-stakes contest with 240 total leagues of 12 and a six-figure grand prize. Reviewing player adds between the two should provide us with a well-rounded perspective and barometer of the fantasy baseball marketplace.
Week 26 Overview
Hitters
The San Diego Padres took advantage of their four-game series with the Rockies at Coors Field and a home set with the Marlins, scoring 51 runs, 12 more than any other team. Fernando Tatis Jr. (along with Brandon Lowe and Pete Crow-Armstrong) led the way with a week-high four dingers. Last week’s streamers turned out to be dynamite: Jake Cronenworth (.464-8-2-8-2), Dustin Harris (.379-5-0-7-2) and Samad Taylor (.556-6-1-7-1) really stepped up, particularly Taylor for my competitive Main Event squad that gained two category points in batting average last week. Rake Cronenworth was true to his nickname from several years ago. He led all Major League hitters with 13 hits. The Brewers swiped a league-high 12 bags last week: four each for Jackson Chourio and rookie Cooper Pratt. Tampa’s Chandler Simpson led all runners with five swipes, finally catching Washington’s Nasim Nuñez for the MLB lead with 46. Expect Simpson to finish with 50+ and win the stolen base crown.
Pitchers
Of the 29 two-start pitchers excluding Pirates opener Lake Bachar, three earned two wins: Tarik Skubal, Sean Burke and David Peterson. Houston’s Hunter Brown had an outstanding two-step (10 IP – 5 H – 1 ER – 5 K – 20 K) and those 20 punchouts led all pitchers for the week. Gavin Williams punched out 16 in 12 innings and is back atop the AL lead in strikeouts with 244. Dylan Cease (239) may not make his final start of the season and Cam Schlittler (234) is unlikely to catch Williams as both have one start remaining. It’s very possible that Williams catches and passes Jacob Misiorowski (247) for the Major League lead. The Miz pitched three innings in his weekend start and might be limited for his final one.
Tampa’s Bryan Baker was the first reliever to reach 40 saves this season. It’s possible that Cade Smith (39), Riley O’Brien (38) and Mason Miller (37) join Baker. The last time there were three closers with 40 or more saves was in 2019: Edwin Díaz (57), Wade Davis (43), and Craig Kimbrel (42). Shout out to folks who drafted O’Brien late, and/or picked up Baker, Louis Varland or Jacob Latz off waivers and didn’t have to worry about the saves category all season.
Week 27 Most Added Players: NFBC Main Event, NFBC OC, and Fantrax
It’s the last hurrah for managers with FAB dollars left, hoping to get the best bang for the buck and for variance to lean their way and tip them into league titles. As is usually the case in the final week, we hope to optimize our pitching rotations and hitters in hitter-friendly ballparks against bad pitching. It was odd seeing Shohei Ohtani available in several leagues, and perhaps fortuitous as he should be activated this week and start a few games. Ohtani was acquired in 26 OCs for an AWB of $17. In Main Events, there were 12 shares available and they went for a reasonable $12 a pop. I scooped up a rare Ohtani share in an OC for $2, winning a tiebreaker over the team in 1st place in that league. Andy Pages will be activated on Tuesday, which should push Tommy Edman back to second base. Pages had been out since August 21, but was producing at an exciting clip before the injury — .272 – 72 R – 21 HR – 80 RBI – 12 SB in 550 PA. Managers who acquired him are hoping that he dusts the cobwebs back off and gets right into the swing of things, with all the marbles on the line.
| # | Player | Team | Position(s) | % of Lgs Added | AWB |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Andy Pages | LAD | OF | 60% | $5 |
| 2 | JR Ritchie | ATL | SP | 57% | $3 |
| 3 | Daniel Lynch IV | KC | SP | 57% | $6 |
| 4 | Samad Taylor | SD | OF | 48% | $5 |
| 5 | Jose Siri | LAA | OF | 45% | $4 |
| 6 | Heliot Ramos | NYY | OF | 35% | $7 |
| 7 | Dansby Swanson | CHC | SS | 35% | $8 |
| 8 | Brayan Bello | BOS | SP | 35% | $11 |
| 9 | Dustin Harris | SD | OF | 32% | $10 |
| 10 | Garrett Whitlock | BOS | RP | 32% | $5 |
| 11 | Pavin Smith | ARI | 1B | 30% | $4 |
| 12 | Anthony Volpe | NYY | SS | 30% | $5 |
AWB = Average Winning Bid (min: $4 AWB)
Pitchers were the most popular targets, specifically two-steppers, as we chase wins and strikeouts, hoping the Ratio Monster doesn’t eat our leads in ERA and WHIP. JR Ritchie and Daniel Lynch IV were the most added starters who we expect two starts from this week. Ritchie’s MLB debut back in April came with great promise, but walks haunted him greatly, which led to trips back to Triple-A to refine his craft and some bulk inning relief work when he returned to Atlanta in July. Ritchie was recently promoted again, and ran into a juggernaut Cubs offense last week, allowing six runs on seven hits in 4.2 innings. The walk rate (13.7%) isn’t pretty, and he has a good opportunity to end his season on a high note with two reasonable matchups — against the Reds at home and the Marlins on the road. Lynch had served the Royals well as their top southpaw out of the bullpen for most of the season. He moved to the rotation in August and slowly worked his pitch counts upward. Lynch has made it to five innings in each of his last three starts. His latest one (at HOU on September 16) went well — 5 IP – 2 H – 0 ER – 1 BB – 3 K. More of that please as he faces the White Sox and Guardians at Kauffman Stadium in the final week. If I could only choose one for the week, it would be Ritchie.
Red Sox pitchers Brayan Bello and Garrett Whitlock were popular buys as the likelihood of roto stars shining bright on them this week is high. Bello is coming off a tremendous outing against the AL-leading Rays on Saturday where he posted an 11:0 K:BB with just one run allowed in eight innings. Those 11 punchies tied his career high. Bello had been the worst starter in the game (6.49 ERA, 1.67 WHIP) through June 4, when he was optioned to Triple-A. Since the All-Star break, mostly out of relief and with two starts, the 27-year-old has been shining. Over those 51.1 innings, he is rocking exemplary ratios (2.28 ERA, 1.01 WHIP) and a 17% K-BB% (22.3% K, 5.3% BB). Bello should make a start against the Cubs next Saturday. The Cubs should be settled into a playoff spot by then, so perhaps they give Pete Crow-Armstrong and some of the other regulars that day off. Boston’s closer Aroldis Chapman has been day-to-day with a lat issue, so perhaps the Red sox have him take it easy and provide Whitlock with some save opportunities. Whitlock has a 7-2 record with a 17.5 ERA, 0.88 WHIP and four saves.
Streaming Diamondbacks is a good idea this week, specifically for their three-game set at Coors Field against the Rockies in the early part of the week. Pavin Smith was a coveted target, coming off a four-day stretch where three of his hits were home runs. Don’t expect Smith to start against lefty Kyle Freeland, but he should be in the lineup for the other two contests against righties. Nolan Arenado was available in one of the 60 Main Event leagues and was acquired for just one dollar.
Better late than never for two punchless Padres who have been quite productive and certainly enjoyed their visit to Coors Field in the first half of last week. Dustin Harris ($10 AWB) and Samad Taylor ($5) have been red hot and playing often over the last 10 days. Though he doesn’t have a home run yet, Harris has been quite productive and helpful to early-bird managers: eight runs, 12 runs batted in and three steals, batting .384 with a 166 wRC+ in 40 plate appearances since September 11. He’s also been batting second against right-handed starters. Taylor has at least one hit in nine of his last 10, including a 3-for-3 effort on Sunday, and has driven in seven in his last seven games.
| # | Player | Team | Position(s) | % of Lgs Added | AWB |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Dustin Harris | SD | OF | 34% | $8 |
| 2 | Cristian Javier | HOU | SP | 33% | $7 |
| 3 | Anthony Kay | CHW | SP | 24% | $10 |
| 4 | Robert Gasser | MIL | SP | 22% | $9 |
| 5 | Daniel Lynch IV | KC | SP | 22% | $7 |
| 6 | Jonah Cox | SF | OF | 22% | $8 |
| 7 | Josh Jung | TEX | 3B | 21% | $6 |
| 8 | Yusei Kikuchi | LAA | SP | 20% | $4 |
| 9 | Max Scherzer | TOR | SP | 18% | $5 |
| 10 | Brayan Bello | BOS | SP | 18% | $12 |
| 11 | Dansby Swanson | CHC | SS | 16% | $7 |
| 12 | Andrew Alvarez | WAS | SP | 16% | $8 |
| 13 | JR Ritchie | ATL | SP | 15% | $5 |
AWB = Average Winning Bid (min: $4 AWB)
As always, more reliable starting pitcher depth was available in the 12-team OC pool. Cristian Javier, Anthony Kay, Robert Gasser, Lynch, Yusei Kikuchi, and Max Scherzer were the most added pitchers this week. Javier should pitch twice this week and will hope to put his best foot forward (in this case, his right arm) as the Astros fight for the AL West and a playoff spot. Sutter Health Park is not a fun place to pitch, but the A’s lineup is a watered-down version without Brent Rooker, Nick Kurtz, Tyler Soderstrom, and Jacob Wilson윌슨. Javier’s first start is in Seattle may not be a picnic with gluten-free granola and Pearl Jam on the Discman.
Milwaukee’s Robert Gasser only draws one start (home vs. STL), but is considered a reliable ratios guy who can score a much-needed win for fantasy managers, as the Brewers will certainly be favorites in that matchup. Gasser earned his fifth win on Saturday, throwing seven scoreless innings against the Orioles. White Sox lefty Anthony Kay has good matchups (at KC on Tuesday and vs. COL on Sunday), though that second start could be pulled away from him. The main problems here is that Kay hasn’t made it to the fifth inning in any of his last five starts. I feel much more comfortable with a single start against the Orioles from Max Scherzer than I do a double (at SEA, at ATH) from wily Yusei Kikuchi. Kikuchi has walked 12 batters in his last three starts.
| # | Player | Team | Position | Roster % | +/- |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Ryan Johnson | LAA | SP | 50% | 12% |
| 2 | Dustin Harris | SD | OF | 18% | 10% |
| 3 | Jack Perkins | ATH | RP | 26% | 7% |
| 4 | Dean Kremer | MIN | SP | 45% | 7% |
| 5 | Ryan Watson | LAA | RP | 10% | 6% |
| 6 | Andrew Alvarez | WSH | SP | 46% | 6% |
| 7 | David Peterson | CHC | SP | 56% | 5% |
| 8 | David Sandlin | CHW | RP | 21% | 5% |
| 9 | Victor Mesa Jr. | TB | OF | 43% | 4% |
| 10 | Leo Bernal | STL | C | 35% | 3% |
| 11 | Javier Sanoja | MIA | 2B,3B,SS,OF | 62% | 3% |
(+/-) is the % of leagues the player was added to in the previous week
It’s possible that attraction towards Ryan Johnson this weekend relates to dynasty and keeper formats, and not his start in Seattle this week. Johnson has limited run damage over his last nine starts, since August 6, posting a 2.39 ERA, but with an xFIP (5.01) nearly double the mark. Johnson is more of a 4.25-4.50 ERA guy than a sub-3.00 ERA one, as his 90.9% LOB and .229 BABIP portends.
Perhaps a similar mindset applies to folks who scooped up Jack Perkins, who pitched two quality starts on the road against the Rays (6.2 IP – 4 H – 0 ER – 1 BB – 8 K) and the Guardians (6 IP – 5 H – 1 ER – 0 BB – 4 K), flashing some of his upside and future potential. Perkins has had a difficult season (5.90 ERA, but a 4.16 xFIP, 1.45 WHIP) and will be a tough streamer at home in Sacramento next season, but the strikeouts (25.2%) should always be there.
Andrew Alvarez should have a rotation spot with the Nationals next season. He has been outstanding since the All-Star break, posting a 2.44 ERA (3.30 FIP, 4.02 xFIP) with a 1.10 WHIP and a 22.7% strikeout rate, though he wasn’t able to secure a win in any of those 10 starts. Alvarez won’t be a particularly coveted target in drafts next season, but should have a NFBC ADP somewhere in the 250-325 overall range. He may be a consideration in NL-only keeper leagues with deep benches and five-plus keepers.
Bold Predictions for Week 27
Gavin Williams and Jacob Misiorowski finish the season tied for the MLB lead in strikeouts with 255. Williams punches out 11 and Misiorowski, eight.
JR Ritchie steps up for his two starts and has a Jack Perkins Week 26 type week, helping managers win league titles.
Cade Cavalli twirls a gem in Detroit this week and pulls his 3.02 ERA under 3.00 to end the season. Cavalli will have a top-60 ADP in 2027.
Jo Adell takes advantage of four left-handed starters this week and earns seven RBIs to reach 100, after falling two RBIs short last season.
One of Cristian Javier or Yusei Kikuchi will remind why streaming pitchers in Sutter Health Park, even if part of a two-step, is a mistake.
Miguel Vargas and Colson Montgomery hit three home runs each this week and the White Sox score the most runs in Week 27.
The Houston Astros win the NL West and knock the Texas Rangers out of playoff contention.
I hope you enjoyed my column this season and that you found it helpful, or at least entertaining and informative. Stay tuned for more from me next week as we hit the offseason streets. Best of luck this final week!
Vlad writes for RotoGraphs and is the head of fantasy baseball content at FTN Fantasy. He is a Tout Wars Expert League champ, member of the CDM Fantasy Sports Hall of Fame and has been nominated for FSWA writing awards six times. Vlad has been playing fantasy baseball since 1995, winning 42 NFBC leagues since 2012 and ranking in the top percentile in NFBC’s Online Championship contest (33% win rate, 52% cash rate; 64 leagues). Much to the chagrin of his colleagues and most baseball aficionados, Vlad is a lifelong Dodgers fan who claims his first gut call at age 9 was Kirk Gibson’s 1988 World Series home run. You can follow him on X and BlueSky @RotoGut.

item.title: [full-count.jp] 山本由伸でもベッツでもない…ド軍だけ“異変” 球団の顔が…最新格付けに漂う違和感
item.dc:creator: Full-Count編集部
item.description: 山本由伸でもベッツでもない…ド軍だけ“異変” 球団の顔が…最新格付けに漂う違和感 MLB公式がチームパワーランキングトップ10を発表した MLB公式インスタグラムが21日（日本時間22日）、最新の「チームパワーランキング」トップ10を発表した。各球団を代表する主力選手が画像として並ぶなか、2位に入ったドジャースの“顔”として選出されたのは意外な選手だった。 1位のブルワーズにはジャクソン・チョーリオ外野手とウィリアム・コントレラス捕手、3位のレイズにはジュニオール・カミネロ内野手、4位のブレーブスにはロナルド・アクーニャJr.外野手、6位のカブスにはピート・クロウ＝アームストロング外野手ら、各チームで目覚ましい活躍を見せる中心選手たちが大々的にフィーチャーされた。 そのなかで異彩を放ったのが、2位に位置付けられたドジャースだ。球団の顔として掲載されたのは、大谷翔平投手でも、ムーキー・ベッツ内野手でも、山本由伸投手でもなく、期待の若手であるホスエ・デポーラ外野手だった。 他球団が主力級やチームの看板選手を当然のように並べるなか、大物スターがずらりと揃うドジャースにあって、まだメジャーでの
item.content:encoded:
山本由伸でもベッツでもない…ド軍だけ“異変” 球団の顔が…最新格付けに漂う違和感
MLB公式がチームパワーランキングトップ10を発表した
MLB公式インスタグラムが21日（日本時間22日）、最新の「チームパワーランキング」トップ10を発表した。各球団を代表する主力選手が画像として並ぶなか、2位に入ったドジャースの“顔”として選出されたのは意外な選手だった。
1位のブルワーズにはジャクソン・チョーリオ外野手とウィリアム・コントレラス捕手、3位のレイズにはジュニオール・カミネロ内野手、4位のブレーブスにはロナルド・アクーニャJr.外野手、6位のカブスにはピート・クロウ＝アームストロング外野手ら、各チームで目覚ましい活躍を見せる中心選手たちが大々的にフィーチャーされた。
そのなかで異彩を放ったのが、2位に位置付けられたドジャースだ。球団の顔として掲載されたのは、大谷翔平投手でも、ムーキー・ベッツ内野手でも、山本由伸投手でもなく、期待の若手であるホスエ・デポーラ外野手だった。
他球団が主力級やチームの看板選手を当然のように並べるなか、大物スターがずらりと揃うドジャースにあって、まだメジャーでの実績が極めて少ないデポーラが選ばれたチョイスには、やや違和感を拭えない。
直近の話題性や若手の抜擢という文脈はあるにせよ、圧倒的な存在感を放つスター選手たちを差し置いた画像選定。豪華絢爛なドジャース陣容のなかで浮き彫りとなった“異例の抜擢”は、思わぬ形で注目を集めることとなった。

item.title: [thebiglead.com] Dodgers activate two key players immediately before big Padres series
item.dc:creator: J P Hoornstra
item.description: With one week left in the MLB regular season, the Los Angeles Dodgers are getting two key players back for a three-game home series against the San Diego Padres. Pitcher Roki Sasaki and center fielder Andy Pages, who have been on the injured list since August, were activated from it on Monday, an off day for the Dodgers and Padres. The two National League West rivals can each clinch something important at Dodger Stadium—a berth in the postseason for San Diego and a first-round bye for Los Angele
item.content:encoded:
With one week left in the MLB regular season, the Los Angeles Dodgers are getting two key players back for a three-game home series against the San Diego Padres.
Pitcher Roki Sasaki and center fielder Andy Pages, who have been on the injured list since August, were activated from it on Monday, an off day for the Dodgers and Padres. The two National League West rivals can each clinch something important at Dodger Stadium—a berth in the postseason for San Diego and a first-round bye for Los Angeles.
Sasaki posted a 3.05 ERA in seven starts after the All-Star break but developed a blister on his throwing hand in August. Pages played in his first All-Star Game in July but fractured a bone in his right hand when he was hit by a 100.2 mph fastball from Pittsburgh Pirates starter Bubba Chandler on Aug. 21.
The Dodgers were able to clinch the National League West without the two players, but both figure to play key roles in October for the defending World Series champions.
Postseason roles
The team lost hard-throwing reliever Edgardo Henriquez to a back injury earlier this month. For all his second-half success as a starter, the Dodgers need Sasaki more in their bullpen as a right-handed complement to left-handers Tanner Scott and Alex Vesia.
Pages, meanwhile, was excelling at the plate and in the field prior to his injury, which required surgery. He’ll have six games to tune up for the postseason—and a chance at redemption for last October.
The Dodgers won the World Series even though Pages had only four hits in 16 postseason games, managing just an .078 batting average across four playoff rounds.
Without Pages, the Dodgers moved veteran utilityman Tommy Edman to center field. Through week’s end, he was slashing .245/.328/.376 (94 OPS+) in 79 games this season.
The Dodgers are also expecting Shohei Ohtani to return during the Padres series, but he isn’t eligible to be activated from the 15-day injured list before Wednesday.
In corresponding 26-man roster moves, pitcher Emmet Sheehan and catcher Eliezer Alfonzo were optioned to Triple-A Oklahoma City.

item.content:encoded:
Shohei Ohtani alcanzó los 310 jonrones en su carrera dentro de las Grandes Ligas, consolidándose como uno de los principales referentes ofensivos del béisbol actual. El japonés continúa ampliando sus registros con los Los Angeles Dodgers.
El japonés superó los 300 cuadrangulares
El pelotero japonés llegó a la histórica cifra de 300 cuadrangulares a principios de julio de 2026, una marca que refleja su impacto desde su llegada a las Grandes Ligas. Desde entonces, Ohtani ha continuado incrementando su cuenta.
Durante la temporada 2026, el jugador de los Dodgers ya suma 30 jonrones, alcanzando nuevamente una cifra que se ha convertido en una constante en su trayectoria dentro de MLB.
Con sus 30 cuadrangulares de 2026, Ohtani consiguió su sexta campaña consecutiva con al menos 30 jonrones. Esta racha comenzó durante su etapa con Los Angeles Angels y se ha mantenido tras su llegada a los Dodgers.
Sus primeros años con Los Angeles
Ohtani conectó 22 jonrones en 2018 y posteriormente registró 18 en 2019. En 2020 sumó siete cuadrangulares, antes de protagonizar una importante explosión ofensiva con 46 jonrones en 2021.
En 2022, el japonés terminó con 34 cuadrangulares, mientras que en 2023 alcanzó los 44. Sus números ofensivos lo mantuvieron como uno de los bateadores más productivos de las Grandes Ligas.
Con Los Angeles Dodgers, Ohtani tuvo campañas de 54 jonrones en 2024 y 55 en 2025, antes de llegar a los 30 cuadrangulares durante 2026. Estos registros explican buena parte de su ascenso hasta los 310 vuelacercas.
El registro histórico de Ohtani
Con los 310 jonrones acumulados hasta agosto de 2026, Shohei Ohtani continúa aumentando su legado en MLB. Su trayectoria incluye temporadas de gran producción tanto con los Angels como con los Dodgers.

item.title: [DodgersBeat] Dave Roberts Hints at Possible October Change at Top of Lineup
item.dc:creator: Steve Webb
item.description: LOS ANGELES, CA — The Dodgers still expect Shohei Ohtani back in the lineup before October, and Dave Roberts made clear Saturday that his first instinct remains to put Ohtani right back atop the batting order. But the manager is also preparing for the possibility that things don’t go exactly according to plan.
